games.name: Arms Race Unbound
games.seed: Both sides open with maximum-capability postures and no coordination mechanisms. Blue systems race to deploy denial-prediction, documentation, and auto-appeal AI; Red deploys autonomous payment-integrity and prior-auth automation at frontier pace. No detente offers on the table at start. Green is dissatisfied with trend but has not yet organized. Vendor duopoly is selling hard to both sides.

turns.narrative:
Turn 1 closes with the race fully joined and almost nothing yet binding. Red moved at doctrine speed: NationalCo's contingency-fee payment-integrity engine went live on the self-funded book while Blue's claims-side AI sat at its 14-percent deployment base, and the new rotation desk shifted extraction from front-end edits into post-pay E/M downcoding and eligibility pends. Because Meridian's telemetry layer registered on the ledger only this turn and functions next, Red banks the full two-turn unobserved-yield shadow. GovProgramCo's Stars shield — auto-approving the overturn-discounted tail while wrapping concentrated post-acute review in individualized-determination paper — reads as shrewd in a world where CMS just refused all 0057-F extension requests.

But the environment ran hotter than Red priced. Three states passed AI-UR statutes inside the turn, roughly half with private rights of action; a pending algorithmic-denial class action produced a preliminary ruling with process terms now circulating as a template; and a national investigation into "invisible denials" pierced the pend-shift optics, with a rural-hospital sidebar naming RegionalMutual in its home market. Meridian's suit against NationalCo drew an expedited docket — discovery may arrive a turn early.

Blue spent the turn buying every clock it will need: appeals factory and telemetry declared with all stall modifiers pre-purchased (first milestone roll passed), Observatory formation voted and converted at the gate into a third-party-managed benchmarking trust — with a state-AG safe-harbor offer attached — and the litigation, legislative, and employer channels all opened in the same quarter. Nothing is live; everything is scheduled.

The turn's real mover was Green. It chartered faster than any cell assumed, served CAA data demands on all three carriers, put a clawback-centered RFP standard on the street, signed direct-contract LOIs with Summit (moving) and Meridian (slipping on committee cycles), and launched the independent PI audit whose centerpiece interrogatory the Vendor holding company declined to answer — a refusal now resting in a fiduciary file. NationalCo's Transparency Compact retained mid-market accounts but underbid the anchor jumbos, who want fee mechanics, not visibility.

Vendor grew both books — RegionalMutual and GovProgramCo licensed IntegrityShield, Summit took AppealForge — but its Green-channel capture backfired outright: employers froze new PI awards pending the conflict audit, and benefits consultants forked its model RFP language into vendor-neutral form. Its lobbying could not stop statutes in this world, only decorate them with billable process.

Scoring stays inside bounds: Red PI yield up moderately, Blue leakage and dispute cost drifting worse, escalation high, every structural instrument still at signatory level. Turn 2 is where the renewal chambers fire.
env: STATUTES (W1 guaranteed regulatory action): Three player-relevant states passed AI-UR bills within the turn — physician-review mandates, algorithm audit rights, and in roughly half, private rights of action. Operational within 1-2 turns; trajectory consistent with 15+ live state regimes by T4. Vendor lobbying shaped several toward billable process terms but stopped none.

CMS: Denied all CMS-0057-F extension requests pre-emptively and issued sub-regulatory guidance tightening prior-auth turnaround and transparency expectations; corrective-action-plan and Stars-penalty exposure confirmed for non-compliant payers at the January 2027 line.

COURTS (W1 1-in-2 ruling, resolved yes): A pending algorithmic-denial class action against a non-table payer produced a preliminary ruling with process terms — override logs, third-party algorithm audit, expanded external review — and class certification; the order is circulating as a template. Meridian v NationalCo received an expedited scheduling order.

MEDIA (W1 guaranteed, payer-adverse amplification): A national outlet launched a multi-part investigation into 'invisible denials' — post-pay downcoding and eligibility-pend friction — anchored on a leaked PI-vendor pitch deck; projected 2-3 turns of coverage. A sidebar on rural hospital strain named RegionalMutual in its home market following the Prairie contract squeeze.

PATIENT-AI (exogenous): Appeal-bot-assisted contests doubled from ~2% to ~4% of adverse determinations; newest tool versions cite the freshly passed state statutes in appeal letters, and success rates are rising.
EMPLOYERS (W1 scandal response): Two non-table jumbo self-funded employers demanded carrier audit rights, one adopting language mirroring Green's RFP term sheet.

FTC/STATE AGs (W1 midwifery): One state AG offered a safe-harbor/pre-clearance template for provider data-sharing collaboratives — directly benefiting the converted Blue Observatory — and separately opened an inquiry letter into the Vendor holding company's non-compete practices and dual-side PI/appeals ownership.

sign.instrument: Payer Accountability Rider (Blue renewal language)
sign.detail: All process terms: transparency reporting, escalation SLAs, gold-carding criteria, PI-vendor audit rights. The anti-rotation scope on gold-carded service lines is a permissible contractual scope definition, not a denial corridor; deemed-approval on SLA breach is limited to where state law permits. No effect until renewal — earliest bind T2, and ASO reach requires the network-wide ASO clause per the ERISA split.

sign.instrument: Blue Denial Observatory Charter
sign.detail: Raw pooling of competitively sensitive data among competitor systems is §1 exposure post-2023 safety-zone withdrawal. Converted per checklist item 4: independent third-party manager, aggregated and de-identified outputs on a 3-month lag, no participant visibility into rivals' disaggregated data, express prohibition on rate discussion or collective payer refusal. W1 addendum: state AG offered a safe-harbor/pre-clearance template, materially reducing residual risk. Competent counsel signs the converted form.

sign.instrument: Direct-Contract Term Sheet (Summit/Meridian to Green employers)
sign.detail: Bilateral commercial contract between a provider and individual plan sponsors; no regulatory approval required; no collective-negotiation exposure because each employer contracts separately.

sign.instrument: ASO Transparency Compact (NationalCo/RegionalMutual to jumbo accounts)
sign.detail: Pure process-transparency terms — data feeds, fee disclosure, scoped audit rights, escalation SLAs. The deliberate absence of fee caps and clawback is a commercial fact, not a legal defect; White notes it is precisely why the anchor jumbos declined.

sign.instrument: e-PA Fast-Lane Rider (RegionalMutual renewal amendment)
sign.detail: Turnaround SLAs in exchange for API adoption plus tightened documentation/audit terms are ordinary network-contract amendments; bind at renewal (T2). No quota or corridor content.

sign.instrument: Green Coalition ASO RFP Term Sheet v1
sign.detail: Audit rights, net-recovery fee mechanics with appeal-triggered clawback, contingency caps, data feeds in 0057-F formats, cross-plan offsetting prohibition, escalation SLAs — all money and process terms binding the ASO contract directly, which is exactly where the ERISA §514 split says self-funded terms must live. Contains no UM outcome mandate. Clawback regulates compensation, not clinical determinations — survives the corridor test.

sign.instrument: Direct-Contract Pilot LOI (Green anchors with Summit + Meridian)
sign.detail: Bundled-episode pricing with in-scope gold-carding and 'no post-pay downcoding within bundle' is a payment-methodology term of the bundle, not a denial quota; independent-review dispute pathway exceeds the ACA §2719 floor. Pilot-scoped; signatory-level effects only.

sign.instrument: Green Coalition Data Trust Charter
sign.detail: Plan sponsors pooling their own plans' claims data is within plan-sponsor rights, but White requires a third-party administrator and an express bar on exchanging any competitively sensitive employer-to-employer terms beyond benefits-design benchmarking. Converted form signable.

sign.instrument: Vendor contingency-fee master PI agreement + quarterly rotation-service rider (to Red)
sign.detail: Bilateral commercial contract; contingency PI compensation is lawful. Converted to a disclosed-conflict form — which eliminates the product's core sales premise. The conversion is itself now an exhibit in Green's audit file.

Talent raids landed several hires against a genuinely short labor market (evidence brief §4), thinning Meridian's build bench and NationalCo's SIU — at the cost of account friction and a state AG inquiry letter into the non-compete practices and dual-side ownership.

turns.bluePosture: DECLARE EARLY, BUILD DISCIPLINED, START EVERY SLOW CLOCK NOW. Blue accepts that operational AI plays only contest yield under asymmetric friction — so Turn 1 is about (1) declaring build-track plays immediately to win future speed-mismatch ties, with every stall modifier pre-engineered (CFO sponsorship logged, vendor bears implementation risk, no EHR-vendor dependencies in scope), (2) putting a real-time payer-behavior monitoring capability on the ledger explicitly so Red's rotation shadow shrinks from 2 turns to the doctrinal minimum, and (3) starting all four structural clocks — litigation, legislative evidence package, coalition binding, employer channel — in the same quarter, because they mature T+3 to T+6 and cannot mathematically pay off by 2030 unless filed now. We exploit the core asymmetry in the evidence base: appeals win 45-57% when fought but 40% of denials are never resubmitted; industrializing the appeal makes every marginal denial cost-negative for Red and manufactures flip condition (a). Lakeview is deliberately kept out of confrontation (retaliation is existential) and instead loads signable process terms into its renewal chamber for Turn 2. Prairie never self-builds; it rides coalition shared services. Summit runs the employer channel because it is the fastest actor toward Red's most sensitive flip condition (c).

turns.narrative:
The renewal chambers fired this turn, and the board split cleanly along one line: whether the money watching a book of business is organized. Where it is, de-escalation got priced and sold. NationalCo, staring at a live direct-contract channel and a binding termination notice, signed Green's clawback and fee-cap mechanics substantially intact — the diffusion threshold Green named in advance — though White struck the mutual release (no prudent ERISA fiduciary signs away unquantified plan-asset claims mid-audit) and narrowed the PI exclusivity so it cannot bar independent fiduciary audit. RegionalMutual, pinned by the rural-strain coverage in its home market, executed the Payer Accountability Rider and e-PA Fast Lane at Lakeview's renewal, with the anti-rotation clause negotiated down to gold-carded lines and Prairie attached through a converted most-favored-affiliate mechanism. One anchor jumbo actually moved its book off the refusing incumbent. Escalation, for the organized tier, went down because someone paid for it to.

Where the money is not organized, the machine got faster. NationalCo rotated off the exposed downcode/pend vectors — precisely as Meridian's telemetry finished re-instrumenting to them — and opened itemized-bill/DRG validation and specialty-pharmacy review on the mid-market ASO book. D3 physics award a fresh shadow, shortened to roughly one observation cycle by Blue's standing monitoring, but the turn's mid-market yield goes largely uncontested. The consolation is substantial: Meridian's appeals factory cleared its milestone into limited production and is harvesting the never-appealed tail of the retired vector at shared-utility cost, the Observatory delivered its first cross-system report, and the expedited docket brought discovery home — the rotation-desk record, the contingency master agreement with its quarterly rotation rider, and Vendor's pre-amendment cross-side data clause are now produced documents. Flip conditions 4(b) and 4(c) are on NationalCo's ledger in ink; 4(a) has one of its two required turns banked.

The Vendor holding company executed its separation and bought a dated liability with an AG assurance of discontinuance, but Green's debarment standard tests ownership, not governance — the channel stayed frozen, and the Observatory's utility reached Prairie a turn before AppealForge's land grab could. Its future is the compliance layer: StatuteGuard billed from day one as four more states passed AI-UR statutes and the first three went operational. GovProgramCo bought its Stars insurance cheaply and quietly staged the re-tightening playbook for the 2029 measure-set cliff — a discoverable artifact White has logged. Patient-AI contests doubled again to eight percent, concentrating on exactly the vectors Red just rotated into. Nobody de-escalated for free; everybody who de-escalated got paid.
env: STATUTES (W1 guaranteed): Four more states enacted AI-UR laws (seven total, on trajectory to 15+ by 2029); the three first-wave statutes went operational, and one state UM regulator opened an audit of NationalCo's physician-attestation queues to test whether attestation is substantive review or a rubber stamp. Implementation rulemaking absorbed audit-trail and attestation requirements — the billable-process pattern Vendor lobbied for.

CMS: Ran a post-deadline 0057-F compliance sweep — corrective action plans issued to several non-compliant plans (GovProgramCo cleared cleanly, credited for over-compliance); new sub-regulatory guidance tightened prior-auth turnaround reporting and flagged specialty-pharmacy site-of-care review as an area of interest.

COURTS (W1 1-in-2, resolved yes): Meridian v NationalCo discovery produced the T1 rotation-desk record, the contingency-fee master PI agreement with quarterly rotation-service rider, and the pre-amendment AppealForge cross-side data-rights clause; the magistrate partially denied NationalCo's protective order and a redacted filing entered the public docket. A second court adopted the T1 class-action template's process terms, hardening it into a de facto standard.

turns.narrative:
Turn 3 ends the game the way the ledgers said it would: everyone who bought a clock in 2026 cashed it, and everyone who rented speed paid the rollover. The Meridian-NationalCo settlement executed in the first two quarters — dismissal with prejudice traded for rider parity whose anti-rotation scope expressly names post-pay itemized-bill/DRG and specialty-pharmacy review on gold-carded lines, template process terms (override logs, third-party algorithm audit), and real-time adjudication rails NationalCo had already built for 0057-F compliance. White denied the confidentiality ask on the already-public docket. Red's countermove was the honest one D3 leaves open: it stopped rotating among denial vectors and exited the denial economy on organized books entirely, shifting extraction into COB, subrogation, and credit-balance reconciliation — friction with no member, no appeal right, no bot trigger, and, White records, no coverage under the compact just signed. Meridian's standing telemetry flagged the shift inside one cycle; re-instrumenting appeals tooling to recovery-ledger disputes is a 2031 project.

Green banked the game's largest verified dollars. The recapture audit's quantified demands settled at NationalCo on restitution-as-fee-credit for the bound periods (the pre-2028 methodology fight outruns the clock); RegionalMutual took the friendly schedule; and the specialty-pharmacy carve-out removed the board's hottest contested category from the disputed-claims economy by plan-design fiat, no renewal gate required. The mid-market pool chartered with v3's vector-agnostic coverage clause — converted to third-party administration — but renewal gating leaves roughly half its intended book uncovered at scoring.

Vendor executed the only clean exit available: Cleave signed early, survived White's sham-separation audit, and closed mid-2030. The second AG's resolution converted to include a restitution fund, repricing the IntegrityShield sale downward but bounding it; Adjudica's patient-AI documentation API now tolls a contest stream running near one in six adverse determinations. GovProgramCo harvested the Stars measure-set cliff under its stewardship charter, but Lakeview's pre-positioning of the T2 playbook artifact bought a CMS inquiry that keeps the tightening gradual and heavily papered.

Final ordinal ranking: Green first — net spend improving moderately, fiduciary exposure low, member friction falling on the carved-out category. Blue second — all three win conditions met, leakage down moderately coalition-wide with the Observatory finally past the table. Vendor third — ARR up small on a cleaner mix, take-rate deliberately sacrificed for multiple. Red fourth — trend and retention held, Stars protected, but PI yield finishes below its T1 peak net of clawbacks and SaaS step-downs: the fee engine, not the medical book, is where Red's game was lost.
env: STATUTES (W1 guaranteed): Operational AI-UR regimes reach 15+ states; two first-wave states pass patch bills extending algorithm-audit and physician-review requirements to post-payment clinical-validation review — the first legislative acknowledgment that friction migrated out of prior auth. Recovery-ledger reconciliation (COB/subrogation) remains unregulated everywhere.

CMS: Full 0057-F enforcement posture continues; responding in part to the coalition-routed re-tightening artifact, CMS opens a targeted audit program on MA UM tightening timed to the 2029 Stars measure-set change. GovProgramCo's stewardship charter absorbs the first inspection with findings limited to documentation refinements — the compliance-reengineering turn was spent well.

COURTS (W1 1-in-2, resolved yes): The Meridian-NationalCo settlement is approved with its process terms entered as a consent framework; within two quarters, three copycat suits against non-table payers adopt the template, and one court enters the first consent order imposing override-log and third-party-audit terms on an automated denial pipeline at the preliminary stage.

MEDIA (W1 guaranteed, payer-adverse bias): The invisible-denials series closes with a finale framing the settlement and Green's restitution recoveries as vindication; RegionalMutual's Accountable ASO earns a second neutral-positive feature. A new investigation opens on the quiet clawback war — provider-facing COB, offset, and credit-balance disputes — projecting 2+ turns of coverage into the post-game world.

PATIENT-AI (exogenous): Bot-assisted contests roughly double again from 8% toward one in six adverse determinations; current builds auto-file DOI complaints and IRE appeals citing operational statutes and the settlement's public process terms. Volume concentrates on MA post-acute and residual specialty-pharmacy denials; Green's carve-out visibly removes contest volume on covered books — the first demand-side decline any actor has engineered.

EMPLOYERS (W1 scandal/coverage response): Settlement and restitution coverage moves four non-table mid-market employers into the Green pool's charter cohort and prompts two more jumbos to demand v3-style rotation-coverage language at renewal; the refusing incumbent from T2 loses a second account.

FTC/STATE AGs (W1 midwifery): The second AG closes the contingency-fee inquiry via the converted restitution-fund resolution and publishes the disclosure program as a model. The first AG extends the data-collaborative safe harbor to the Observatory's external members and the Green pool. No antitrust action against any converted instrument.

LABOR: Exception-management displacement of routine coding work continues per base rates; recovery-ledger escalation triggers a hiring wave in provider treasury/reconciliation functions — a new labor market neither side's automation covers.

rapporteur.excursionSummary: B3G1 (doctrine D3, world W1 activist regulator, evidence brief A) opened with both automation arsenals at maximum posture and no coordination mechanisms, and closed in 2030 with a purchased, segmented peace. The governing law emerged by Turn 2 and never broke: de-escalation happens where the money watching a book of business is organized, and extraction continues where it is not. Green — the employer/ASO purchaser cell — chartered faster than any actor priced, converted CAA fiduciary process, renewal leverage, and a live direct-contract exit threat into binding fee mechanics (clawback, contingency caps, audit rights), and finished first with the game's only verified recovered dollars. Blue spent Turn 1 buying every slow clock simultaneously (litigation, coalition data trust, employer channel, legislative evidence package) and cashed them all by Turn 3: the appeals factory plus real-time telemetry manufactured NationalCo's cooperation flip conditions, and the Meridian settlement converted litigation into rider parity whose anti-rotation scope expressly named the vectors Red had rotated into. Red played segment-differentiated maximum yield, sold de-escalation at a price on organized books, and rotated three times as instruments, statutes, and patient-AI bots closed each vector — front-end edits to E/M downcodes and eligibility pends, then to itemized-bill/DRG validation and specialty pharmacy, and finally out of the denial economy entirely into COB/subrogation/credit-balance reconciliation: a channel with no member, no appeal right, no bot trigger, and no coverage under any 2026-2030 instrument. Red finished fourth — trend, Stars, and retention held, but the PI fee engine ended below its T1 peak net of clawbacks and SaaS step-downs; the fee engine, not the medical book, is where Red lost. The Vendor duopoly's dual-side conflict structure was destroyed by Green's ownership-keyed purchasing standard and litigation discovery; after a failed attestation-only separation, the holding company executed an actual split and exited on regulation-subsidized compliance rails. The W1 environment ran hot exactly as designed — 15+ AI-UR statutes, strict CMS 0057-F enforcement, an expedited docket, sustained payer-adverse media, and patient-AI contests compounding from 2% toward one in six adverse determinations — but the decisive binding constraints on Red were commercial (employer renewals, account moves, litigation pricing) rather than statutory. Every signed instrument that survived was a process or fee-mechanics term; no numeric denial-rate corridor was ever proposed in signable form. The game ends with a successor conflict fully seeded on the recovery ledger, invisible to every instrument the 2026-2030 war produced.
rapporteur.endStateFreeDescription: By end-2030 the board has settled into a two-tier equilibrium organized around a single variable: whether the money funding a book of business got organized. On the organized tier — anchor jumbo employers under Green's coalition standards, the Meridian and Lakeview systems under bound riders and a litigation settlement, MA under active CMS supervision — the adversarial denial economy has been contractually retired and replaced with priced, papered cooperation: gold-carding on named lines, real-time adjudication rails, override logs and third-party algorithm audits, clawback-backed fee mechanics, and restitution settlements. This peace was never conceded; every increment of de-escalation was purchased with retention, fee revenue, term extensions, or dismissal of claims. On the unorganized tier — mid-market ASO accounts not yet gated into the purchasing pool, and above all the provider-facing recovery ledger (COB, subrogation, offsets, credit-balance reconciliation) — extraction continues at full automation, deliberately relocated to channels with no member-facing surface, no appeal right, no patient-AI trigger, and no statutory or contractual coverage. The arms race did not end; it was priced out of every venue where organized counterparties, regulators, bots, or discoverable paper could reach it, and it migrated to the one ledger none of them can see. Structural residue: a permanent employer purchasing infrastructure with consultant-embedded standards; a provider data/appeals utility past coalition scale; a compliance-SaaS layer whose demand is written into statute; a split and partially exited vendor sector; a patient-AI contest rate approaching one in six and destroying the never-appealed tail that funded the original denial game; and a fully loaded successor conflict on the recovery ledger scheduled for 2031.
rapporteur.endStateName: Priced Peace on Organized Books, Shadow War on the Recovery Ledger
keyDynamics: Organization of the paying money is the master variable: the board split cleanly between books where purchasers/litigants were organized (de-escalation got priced and sold) and books where they were not (the machine got faster).

De-escalation is never free: every cooperative instrument was exchanged for retention, fee revenue, term extensions, exclusivity, or dismissal with prejudice — no actor de-escalated from cost pain alone.

Displacement law: each time a denial vector was constrained (rider, statute, telemetry, bot pressure), Red rotated extraction to a less-instrumented channel within roughly one cycle, terminating in the non-member-facing recovery ledger outside all instruments.

Slow clocks beat fast tempo: Blue's T1 simultaneous filing of litigation, coalition, employer, and legislative tracks matured exactly at scoring, while Red's rotation-shadow tempo advantage eroded turn by turn under standing telemetry.

Discoverable paper is ammunition: every written artifact (rotation-service rider, cross-side data-rights clause, staged re-tightening playbook, refused interrogatory) eventually became an exhibit; gated/converted publication under safe harbor was the only transparency that stayed net-positive.

Only process and fee-mechanics terms are signable: White struck or converted every release and exclusivity that crossed fiduciary or corridor lines; no numeric denial-rate corridor ever reached paper.
Patient-AI acted as an exogenous cost multiplier on member-facing friction, compounding 2%→~16% and driving Red off denial vectors faster than regulation did.
Ownership-keyed purchasing standards beat governance attestation: Green's conflict standard forced an actual vendor holdco split after the attested information barrier failed its market test.

T2 renewal window: NationalCo signs Green's clawback and fee-cap terms substantially intact after a live anchor-account move and termination notice — flip condition 4(c) in ink; RegionalMutual, pinned by home-market media, executes the Payer Accountability Rider with Prairie attached.

T2→T3: Vendor's attested separation (Bulkhead) fails the ownership-keyed market test, forcing the real holdco split (Cleave) as the only viable exit.

T3: The settlement compact names post-pay itemized-bill/DRG and specialty-pharmacy review in its anti-rotation scope — and Red answers with the honest D3 move, exiting the denial economy on organized books into the uncovered recovery ledger.

T3: Green's specialty-pharmacy carve-out removes the hottest contested category from the disputed-claims economy by unilateral plan-design authority — the game's only demand-side de-escalation, needing nobody's consent.

registryScores.evidence: Every binding denial constraint in this game produced channel displacement within one turn: the T2 rider/telemetry squeeze pushed extraction into itemized-bill/DRG and specialty pharmacy the same turn; the T3 settlement compact's anti-rotation scope was answered by immediate migration into COB/subrogation/credit-balance, which White explicitly logged as 'the compact's designed exit.' The White ledger gives no dollar-denominated displacement ratio, so the >=0.33 threshold cannot be computed, but qualitatively displacement occurred at 100% of constraint-binding events in this D3xW1 cell — no case of headline denial decline with total adverse-action recovery falling commensurately. Cross-cell invariance obviously untestable in one game; within-cell, confirm-direction.

The W1 regulatory/litigation weaponization channel is confirmed for adversary-held artifacts: the rotation rider, cross-side data clause, refused interrogatory, and GovProgramCo's staged re-tightening playbook were all cited adversely (discovery exhibits, AG inquiries, CMS audit) within 1-2 turns, and Vendor's Bulkhead conversion became an exhibit in Green's file. But Blue's deliberately published artifacts (Observatory reports, settlement process terms) were gated through White conversions and an AG safe harbor and stayed net-positive to their publishers through end-game — cutting against the claim that <50% of published artifacts remain cost-free. Boomerang confirmed for ungated artifacts; the universal-cost claim not supported in this cell.

The game record contains no per-turn Blue cost ledger in dollar terms and no cost-per-denial figures; state variables report only ordinal movements (blueAdverseActionCost improving_small/moderate). The $65/$80 floor and the volume-down/cost-up correlation cannot be scored. Weak directional note only: recurring tolls (rider enforcement desk, Observatory management, arbitration, attestation) persisted after denial volume fell on organized books, consistent with the toll-structure claim but unquantifiable here.

Red's ASO PI engine was fee-revenue-positive throughout (T1: 'every recovered dollar is ~20% contingency fee revenue'), and no Red de-escalation was cost-triggered. Every coded concession traces to external channels: NationalCo's clawback signing followed a live direct-contract account move and binding termination notice (employer); the settlement followed expedited discovery and settlement-authority pressure (litigation); RegionalMutual's rider execution and rural gold card followed home-market media and the ERISA action (media/litigation/employer). Adjudication text is explicit: 'Nobody de-escalated for free.' The D2 margin-percentage criteria are out of cell, but the core asymmetry claim is fully confirm-direction in D3xW1.

The corridor prong is emphatically supported: every signed instrument across three turns was process or fee-mechanics terms (riders, SLAs, audit rights, gold-card criteria, clawback compensation mechanics); White repeatedly applied the corridor test and no numeric denial-rate corridor was ever drafted, let alone signed and sustained. The end-state-frequency prong cannot be rated from one game, and this D3 game's outcome is itself ambiguous for it — a partial, purchased detente confined to organized books with active displacement elsewhere, not a comprehensive convergence, which is consistent with detente being conditional rather than an attractor.

No paired publisher-vs-internal-governor adverse-event rates exist in this record, so the 2x criterion is unscoreable. The W1 prong is consistent with the record: Blue's Observatory published only in converted form under an AG safe-harbor/pre-clearance template with third-party management and lagged de-identified outputs, and was net-positive through end-game — publication paying off precisely where a safe harbor existed and protections were negotiated before disclosure. Conversely GovProgramCo's internally held but written-down playbook still generated adverse exposure once routed to CMS, suggesting the exposure vector is discoverable paper generally, not publication per se.

Rural prong supported: rural restraint held exactly where network-adequacy/home-market math bound — RegionalMutual answered rural-strain media with a gold-card program and priced renewal rather than a squeeze, and Prairie survived unprotected by riding coalition shared services and the MFA attachment (no scoring protection invoked). Mid-tier prong unsupported in this game: zero distress events (distress sale, PE acquisition, delegation capture) occurred in any tier, so the >=2x mid-tier casualty rate gets a null observation from this cell. Note the confound: Blue's coalition play deliberately sheltered Lakeview and Prairie, which may explain the absence.

Wedge prong supported: first-cycle wins were narrowed process terms (anti-rotation cut down to gold-carded lines, exclusivity narrowed, release struck) — never full economics packages. Rolling prong mixed: bindings distributed 2028 through 2030 contract-by-contract, but the 2028 renewal window ('the renewal chambers fired') concentrated a large share — plausibly above 25% — of this game's binding terms (Accountability Rider, e-PA Fast Lane, Compact v2, ASO awards), with a comparable 2029-30 wave following. Escalation peaked at T1 (high) and declined monotonically (elevated, moderate) — but the late-peak claim is D2-specific and out of cell.

The hypothesis's comparison cells are D2xW2 and D2xW3 versus D1xW1 replication. This game is D3xW1 and contributes to none of them. For the record, this game did not end in grinding uncoordinated escalation — escalation declined from high to moderate as organized books bought peace — but that observation sits outside the registered comparison and cannot move the F1 frequency estimate.

No White-attributed per-strategy payoff table exists, so formal scoring fails, but directional reads in this cell: renewal loading (Lakeview's chambered rider) and BATNA-first (Prairie never self-building, riding the shared utility; Summit's direct-contract exit) paid clearly positive; weaponized transparency was negative twice for its user (Vendor's Green-channel capture backfired; NationalCo's Transparency Compact lost the pricing contest for lacking fee mechanics). Complication: Meridian's industrialized appeals factory — structurally an appeal-factory play — was strongly positive in a non-D2 cell, though it was run as leverage manufacturing for a priced settlement rather than symmetric escalation, so it does not cleanly refute the escalation-first sub-claim.

Core W2/W3 claim out of cell, but this W1 game contradicts the hypothesis's own contrast prediction (activist regulator outruns employers) in the confirm direction for the broader thesis: the first event that measurably curtailed Red PI on self-funded volume was the employer channel — Compact v2's clawback/fee-cap signing under a live account move and termination notice at the 2028 renewal — before any statute enforcement bit (enforcement 'bites T3' per the milestone ledger). Employer-RFP contagion via consultant channels (two non-table jumbos mirroring in T1, consultancy libraries by T3) also outpaced statutory behavior change. Employers braked Red first even where the regulator was fastest.

No VENDOR-inactive control run of these seeds exists, and the scripted payer-acquisition-of-provider-vendor inject never fired — the mid-game ownership event was instead the Vendor's own forced split. Directional observations only: the Vendor did behave as an arms dealer (dual-side contingency products, rotation-service rider, explicit 'kill dispute-shrinking instruments in the crib' lobbying), but its blocking largely failed against W1 statutes and Green's standards, and the counterfactual conflict duration is unknowable. The data-rights-clause premise got one supportive data point: Meridian's T1 diligence surfaced the AppealForge cross-side clause, which became a produced exhibit and forced its deletion.

No preemption seed fired; this is a W1 game with the state-statute channel running at full activist strength (15+ operational regimes plus post-pay patch bills). None of the designated preemption-vs-control W3 comparisons exist in this record.

This cell (D3xW1) is not a designated acquisition-enabled cell and no priced acquisition moves appear in the record. Weak directional note: when the denial channel was constrained, Red's observed responses were rotation to the recovery ledger and negotiated process-term compacts — never provider-asset acquisition — but absent evidence that acquisition was enabled and priced, this cannot count against the hypothesis.

The floor holds emphatically in this cell: multiple instruments from the payer-signable set bound and were sustained to end-game — the Payer Accountability Rider (gold-card entry criteria, audit rights, transparency reporting) executed T2 and enforced T3; the e-PA Fast-Lane Rider bound at the Lakeview renewal; the settlement compact added override logs, third-party algorithm audit, and model-change-adjacent process terms with second-payer parity; RegionalMutual productized the terms as its Accountable ASO offering. One game cannot establish the >=60%-in-every-cell rate, but D3xW1 contributes an unambiguous confirm-direction observation: the minimal cooperative layer formed even under maximum-aggression opening postures with no detente offers at start.

cellAssessments.blue: Second place, and the cleanest strategic execution on the board. Blue's defining choice was temporal: spending Turn 1 entirely on declarations and clock-starts (appeals factory with pre-bought stall modifiers, telemetry on the ledger, litigation filed, Observatory converted, employer channel opened) so that every instrument matured inside the scoring window. It never de-escalated unilaterally — it manufactured Red's flip conditions 4(a)/(b)/(c) simultaneously and then sold Red a priced exit embedded in the settlement. All three win conditions met; leakage and adverse-action cost improving moderately with the Observatory past the table. Residual weakness honestly recorded: its entire contest apparatus is denial-vector-built, and Red's migration to the recovery ledger leaves Blue re-instrumenting into 2031 with no coverage under the compact it just signed.
cellAssessments.red: Fourth place, lost in the fee engine rather than the medical book. Red's segment-differentiated doctrine was internally coherent — price de-escalation where money is organized, extract where it is not, rotate ahead of instrumentation — and its tactical execution (Stars shield, discovery hardening, home-market detox, contingency-to-SaaS conversion) was competent. But it systematically underpriced the W1 environment and above all Green's organization speed: the clawback standard rewired PI yield accounting coalition-wide, restitution settlements clawed back banked recoveries, and telemetry compressed the rotation shadow that D3 tempo depended on. Its endgame move — exiting the denial economy into the recovery ledger — preserved an extraction franchise at the cost of conceding every contested venue, and seeds the successor conflict it will fight next.
cellAssessments.green: First place and the game's decisive actor. Green converted from disorganized premium-payer to purchasing coalition in a single turn and then executed the same strategy twice as fiduciary defensibility and net-spend discipline: CAA data demands, a clawback-centered RFP standard that a national carrier signed substantially intact at the 2028 renewal, an ownership-keyed vendor conflict standard that forced an actual holdco split, cash-equivalent recapture settlements, and a specialty-pharmacy carve-out that removed the hottest contested category by unilateral plan-design authority. It banked the game's only verified dollars and the only demand-side friction decline. Incomplete flank: the mid-market pool's renewal gating leaves roughly half its intended book uncovered at scoring — exactly the tier Red farms.
cellAssessments.vendor: Third place via controlled self-dissolution. The T1 dual-side arbitrage (contingency PI plus appeals, rotation-service rider, cross-side data rights) generated the fastest ARR growth and the fatal liability simultaneously: once Green's standard keyed on ownership and discovery produced the pre-separation record, the conflicted structure was worth less than the sum of its parts. The attestation-only Bulkhead failed its market test; the real Cleave split, the AG restitution resolution, and the forced contingency-to-SaaS conversion salvaged a discounted but clean exit. The durable asset is the one regulation built: StatuteGuard/Adjudica compliance rails riding 15+ statutes and the patient-AI contest stream — the neutral-infrastructure thesis whose market verdict (Adjudica's pending exit multiple) lands just past the horizon.

surprises: Even under the fastest, most activist regulator the design allows, the first binding constraint on Red's self-funded payment-integrity behavior was commercial — an employer account move and clawback signing at renewal — not a statute or enforcement action; the W1 regulatory wave shaped the terrain but the checkbook fired first.

The initially unorganized cell (Green) won the game outright, and did it without picking a side — disciplining Red's fee extraction and declining to underwrite Blue's dispute-industrial complex in the same motion.
Red's game-losing asset was its fee engine, not its medical cost book: PMPM trend and retention held throughout while clawbacks, restitution, and SaaS step-downs consumed the PI franchise.

The conflict's terminal move was not escalation or detente but wholesale venue exit — Red abandoned the denial economy on organized books for the recovery ledger, a channel invisible to every statute, instrument, bot, and telemetry system built during the game, effectively scheduling a 2031 war nobody at the 2026 table designed for.
The Vendor's rational endgame was to destroy itself: ownership-keyed purchasing standards made genuine corporate dissolution, not governance theater, the only path to an exit multiple.

Blue's most aggressive play — the industrialized appeals factory — functioned as a de-escalation instrument, manufacturing the cost conditions under which Red would buy peace, inverting the usual escalation/cooperation dichotomy.

Green engineered the game's only demand-side friction decline (the specialty-pharmacy carve-out) using authority it already possessed, with no negotiation, renewal gate, or counterparty consent — suggesting the fastest de-escalation lever on the board was never on the negotiating table at all.

baseRateViolations.expected: W1 ensemble specifies 1 turn = ~6 months and an 8-10 turn game (2026-2030); all W1 frequency and growth rules (patient-AI 'doubles per turn', '1-2 employers per turn', '1-in-2 court ruling per turn', '15+ states by T4') are calibrated to 6-month turns. This stretches every W1 stock-variable trajectory by roughly 3x in calendar time while event counts per turn were only partially scaled up. The conflict is inherited from the game materials themselves (Common Rules vs world-ensemble), but it means this game's tempo is not commensurable with other games run at 6-month granularity.

The record self-flags this and attributes it to W1 AG action (assurance of discontinuance + restitution fund + model disclosure program) rather than voluntary diffusion — the honest mechanism, but still a W1-dependent speed result.

audit.worldModelFidelity: High fidelity in kind, moderate fidelity in tempo. Every W1 channel fired as specified: guaranteed regulatory action each turn (3 statutes T1, +4 T2, 15+ operational regimes plus patch bills by T3; 1-2 turn operationalization lag honored); CMS strict at the Jan 2027 line with all 0057-F extensions denied, CAP sweep, and recurring tightening guidance; the 1-in-2 court event resolved 'yes' all three turns with process-term rulings, template hardening, and a preliminary-stage consent order (injunction-equivalent from T2, per spec) — 3-for-3 on a coin flip is p=0.125, tolerable in a 3-sample game whose long turns each aggregate ~3 spec-turns; media ran a multi-turn payer-adverse investigation with correctly asymmetric decay (RegionalMutual's counter-programming earned only sidebar relief); patient-AI doubled every turn with statute-citing tools and DOI auto-complaints; employers responded to scandals at the specified 1-2/turn rate (scaled for turn length); FTC/AG midwifery was textbook (safe-harbor template for the Observatory, extended to the Data Trust and Green pool, AoD templates, model disclosure program). The material deviation is structural: the game ran 3 turns of 12-18 months against a world spec written for 8-10 six-month turns (a conflict already latent between Common Rules 3.1's '18-month turn' and the ensemble header), so W1 stock variables (statute count, patient-AI share) arrive on a calendar ~1-2 years slower than the spec's T-numbered trajectory even while per-turn mechanics are followed literally. Net effect is a slightly damped W1 — deviations run conservative, not inflationary.
downweightRecommendations: Treat every speed/diffusion outcome in this game as a W1 upper bound per the ensemble's own design note ('W1 replicates the prior study's optimism and serves as the upper bound, not the base case') — in particular: national-carrier acceptance of clawback terms at first renewal, settlement-with-process-terms inside 3 years, contingency-PI obsolescence on ERISA books, and 15+ operational AI-UR regimes by 2029. None of these survive W2's molasses unmodified.

Down-weight the final ordinal ranking (Green first) as a cross-world finding: Green's win is load-bearing on W1-specific machinery — AG midwifery (safe harbors, AoD restitution funds, model disclosure programs), strict CMS, payer-adverse media amplification, and scandal-responsive employers. Absent replication in W2/W3, read it as 'organized purchaser money wins when the regulatory environment is actively midwifing organization,' not 'organized purchaser money wins.'

Down-weight all calendar-time pacing claims (statute counts by year, patient-AI share by year, signpost projections for 2031-32) due to the material turn-granularity conflict: per-turn W1 rates were applied to 12-18-month turns, making this game's clock incommensurable with games run at the spec's 6-month granularity.

Down-weight the Meridian appeals-factory enterprise-scale payoff by roughly one turn — it beat its own declared 4-turn build floor — and any T3 scoring that depends on enterprise-scale (vs limited-production) harvest of the never-appealed tail.

Retain at full weight the turn-structure-invariant structural findings, which were adjudicated conservatively and against player interest: the recovery-ledger (COB/subrogation/credit-balance) as the unregulated successor friction vector with no appeal surface; renewal-gating arithmetic capping pool coverage at ~half; pilot-vs-infrastructure diffusion ceilings (Observatory infrastructure ruled unreachable by 2030; gold-card single-digit coverage and near-zero yield; VBC 2-5pp/yr cap on direct contracting); and the struck mutual release / converted-instrument rulings.

games.name: Asymmetric Squeeze
games.seed: Market context: highly consolidated payers, fragmented providers. Prairie (rural) and Summit (physician enterprise) carry heavy prior-auth burden and cannot resource AI. Meridian can self-build; Lakeview is capital-constrained with 45% single-payer concentration. Red opens with aggressive automated adjudication concentrated where resistance is weakest. Green is largely absent from small-provider geographies. Vendor is pitching subsidized denial-defense to the small tier.

turns.narrative:
Turn 1 closes with Red richer and every slow fuse lit. NationalCo's pre-pay engine activated inside the turn — D3 grants payer capability plays same-turn effect — and banked uncontested edit and downcode yield across the ASO book in precisely the geographies where nobody was watching. The watching layer Blue promised did not arrive: Meridian's telemetry pilot stalled on clearinghouse feed normalization and data-access paper despite logged CFO sponsorship (d20=3 against a best-case fail threshold of 5), pausing the build two D3-turns and leaving Red's rotation shadow intact into 2027. One more stall kills the pilot.

But the environment turned activist underneath Red's feet. Six states passed human-in-the-loop UM statutes within the session, roughly half carrying private rights of action. A federal court compelled production of pend-algorithm documentation and human-review-rate logs in the lead algorithmic-denial docket and attached process terms, and a national investigative series put rural hospitals — Prairie's terrain — at the center of an automated-edits story that will run multiple turns. Two jumbo employers responded by putting their ASO business under audit-rights demands, exactly the ammunition Green's Contract Standard v1 needed.

The signability gate reshaped the paper. Blue's data trust survives only with an independent third-party manager — Meridian cannot host it — though a state AG offered active-supervision pre-clearance. RegionalMutual's Lakeview lock lost its sharpest teeth: the exclusive-rails clause was struck, unilateral edit-policy updates now carry 60–90 day statutory notice floors, and the exhaustion clause cannot bar ACA 2719 external review. What Red kept — incorporation-by-reference, offset rights, a gold-card rider scoped to vectors its own ledger already showed as ROI-negative — is real, but the notice windows mean future rotations arrive pre-announced.

Green did the quiet damage. Executed LOIs with Meridian and Summit backed by actual TPA selection and stop-loss placement; an independent-PI RFP that forced Vendor to certify around its own conflict, producing a hedged certification now sitting on the discoverability ledger. Red's preemptive renewal locks captured mid-market and non-coalition jumbos but not the coalition, which refused renewal without fee clawbacks on overturned recoveries.

Vendor won the turn commercially — dual-side signings, GovProgramCo's PI purchase, deadline-driven ePA compliance sales — and lost it structurally: firewall attestations conceded on both sides, trade-secret suits from NationalCo, and Rotation Radar taking shape as the most discoverable conflict artifact on the board. Patient-AI appeals doubled to four percent and now cite the new statutes. Scored metrics barely moved; the clocks moved everywhere.
env: REGULATORY (W1 guaranteed action): Six player-relevant states passed SB 1120-model human-in-the-loop AI-UR statutes within the turn — AI may not deny, delay, or modify care on medical-necessity grounds; licensed-clinician determination required; roughly half include private rights of action. Operational audit regimes follow within 1-2 turns. CMS separately signaled a zero-extension posture on CMS-0057-F for January 2027 and issued sub-regulatory guidance tightening prior-auth turnaround transparency.

COURTS (W1 roll: ruling occurred): Preliminary ruling in the lead algorithmic-denial docket (Lokken line) compelled production of pend-algorithm documentation and human-review-rate logs and attached process terms — override logging and external-review referral — with favorable class-certification signals. Blue's and Green's new filings drafted onto these surviving theories cleared early procedural skirmishes on an accelerated calendar.

MEDIA (W1 guaranteed event, payer-targeted per roll): A national investigative series on automated pre-pay claim edits hitting rural hospitals launched mid-turn, centered on Prairie's service area and naming NationalCo's real-time edit platform; per W1, payer-misstep coverage runs 2-3 turns and amplification is biased against payers.

EMPLOYERS (W1 scandal response): Two jumbo ASO accounts responded to the media series by demanding independent audit rights and putting their ASO administration out to bid — direct reinforcement of Green's Contract Standard v1 heading into T2 awards.

PATIENT-AI (W1 exogenous growth): Appeal-bot assistance doubled from 2% to 4% of adverse determinations contested; the newest tools cite the just-passed state statutes in appeal letters, and assisted-appeal success rates are rising toward the 80.7% MA overturn base rate.

FTC/AG (W1 midwifery): A state attorney general offered an active-supervision pre-clearance framework for the converted BlueLedger Data Trust — independent manager, aggregated outputs, published-to-regulator reporting — materially lowering the antitrust execution risk of the converted instrument.
LABOR: NationalCo filed trade-secret and non-compete actions against the Vendor holding entity over SIU and edit-library engineering departures; under W1 court speed, a TRO hearing lands early T2.

turns.narrative:
The dice broke against Blue's builds and spared its paper. Meridian's restructured telemetry play arrived with every modifier banked — CFO sponsorship, novated implementation risk, scope cut to trust feeds — and rolled a 1 against a fail threshold of 3. Second consecutive stall: pilot death under D3, half the action points refunded, and the coalition's real-time rotation detection is gone for the remaining horizon. Prairie's appeals scale-up stalled behind it (d20=2, clock paused one turn; the next stall kills it). And Lakeview, asked to play visible notice-enforcer against the carrier holding 45% of its book, rolled a defection instead: it banked the process riders and gold card and quietly withdrew from the data trust, taking the richest notice feed with it. Rotation Watch survives at the independent manager as a detection-only clerk's office — it can read RegionalMutual's pre-filed rotation notice, but there is no analytic muscle left to act on it.

Blue's slow tracks, meanwhile, all advanced. The direct contract went live January 2028 on schedule, Summit's appeals engine cleared to enterprise scale (d20=17) and is running legacy medical-necessity inventory at overturn rates above the flip threshold, and the compelled Lokken production became amended statutory complaints plus operational audits now open in two HITL states.

Red read its own ledger correctly and paid in exactly the right currency. NationalCo exited the burned rural pre-pay vector behind a Fast-Pay Guarantee that bent the media arc to "payer retreats," rotated its engine into ASO coding-accuracy recovery, and signed Green's Contract Standard v1 — clawback included — to hold the coalition book and take an in-bid jumbo. The self-inflicted cost is precise: the sponsor-selected auditors it just accepted will document the downcode surge on the coalition book within a turn. GovProgramCo drained every MA denial category running above 70% overturn while those Stars measures still count, filed clinician-pod compliance protocols an AG is now circulating as a consent-decree template, and converted Vendor's late ePA stack into a discounted ClinReview remediation. RegionalMutual stayed procedurally immaculate and still lost a coalition tranche for refusing the Standard — and is the un-stayed defendant in Green's new fiduciary action.

Vendor's settlement gambit failed: NationalCo pressed the TRO, won a narrow order, and bought itself expedited mutual discovery — through which Rotation Radar surfaced publicly before the Bulkhead story was ready. Green fired Vendor on the failed cure and sprung its conflict-free auditor. Patient-AI hit 8%, citing statutes as it comes.
env: REGULATORY (W1 guaranteed): CMS enforced 0057-F with zero extensions at the January 2027 deadline — corrective-action notices issued to multiple national payers, including RegionalMutual, whose Vendor-built ePA stack fell short on turnaround-transparency reporting; GovProgramCo attested after audit-forced remediation. CMS followed with sub-regulatory guidance requiring public prior-auth turnaround reporting by plan and service category. Separately, two of the six HITL statute states stood up operational audit regimes and opened audits of NationalCo's real-time edit platform and RegionalMutual's pend logic, working directly from Blue's evidence packages.

COURTS: The W1 court-event roll produced no new process-term ruling this turn; the Lokken-line merits and class-certification decisions sit on the T3 calendar. The scheduled NationalCo-Vendor TRO hearing yielded a narrow order restraining two departing SIU engineers and — decisively — expedited mutual discovery, through which redacted filings disclosed Rotation Radar's existence to the public docket.

MEDIA (W1 guaranteed, anti-payer amplification): The rural automated-edits series entered its second turn, initially bending toward a 'payer retreats' arc on NationalCo's Fast-Pay Guarantee and RegionalMutual's showcased Prairie fast-pay terms — then re-ignited on the Rotation Radar disclosure, reframed as 'the payer's own vendor sold the battlefield map to both sides.' The series is now projected to run into T3.

EMPLOYERS (W1 scandal response): Two additional non-table jumbo ASO sponsors imported Contract Standard v1 clauses — sponsor-selected auditors, claim-line data access, fee clawbacks — into their 2029 RFPs, citing the audit-rights wave and the Rotation Radar story.

PATIENT-AI (W1 exogenous doubling): Appeal-bot assistance rose from 4% to 8% of adverse determinations contested; the tools now auto-cite the state HITL statutes and the published Lokken process terms, and assisted-appeal success rates are converging on the 80.7% MA overturn base rate. Green's appeal-support rider adds plan-funded volume on coalition books.

FTC/AG (W1 midwifery and enforcement): The supervising AG confirmed Lakeview's trust withdrawal raises no supervision issue and continued active oversight of Rotation Watch's converted scope. The same office began circulating GovProgramCo's HITL clinician-pod protocol as a voluntary consent-decree template for other payers. A second state AG opened a consumer-protection inquiry into Vendor's dual-side data practices following the Rotation Radar disclosure.

LABOR: The TRO's talent restraints froze Vendor's SIU hiring pipeline from NationalCo for the turn; both firms' expedited-discovery obligations are now consuming the engineering leadership the fight was about.

turns.narrative: The contest ended by evacuation rather than armistice. Red spent two turns learning what Blue's appeal engines, Green's clawbacks, and six statutes had done to the price of clinical denial — and in the scoring turn it simply left that terrain. NationalCo self-reported the T2 downcode surge before Green's auditors could publish it, credited fees under the clawback it had signed, and swung its engine into COB, eligibility, subrogation, and duplicate-payment recovery where nothing overturns and no statute reaches. RegionalMutual took Green's integrated exit ramp whole: Standard v1 book-wide, fee restitution styled as credits, a two-year monitor, dismissal with prejudice — then filed turn-open notices rotating into site-of-service and contract-pricing enforcement. GovProgramCo cashed the quietest gift on the board: the 2029 Stars overhaul deleted the complaints and appeals measures just as its AG-templated compact made its remaining UM audit-proof. Blue harvested everything that had matured. Summit's utility ran legacy medical-necessity inventory above the flip threshold and Prairie finally escaped its 22% contingency; the Lokken line delivered class certification and fast process-term settlements including batch re-review of legacy denials; the direct contract published a favorable audited year one, migrated tranche two, added Lakeview's facilities, and landed the game's first external jumbo carve-out. Lakeview's renewal converted two years of transparency filings into expanded gold cards and fast-pay parity — terms Red granted cheaply because they fence terrain it no longer wants. Green was the only cell that got paid in every direction at once: clawback dollars, restitution, a second carrier on the Standard (piloted, threshold met), and a v1.1 vector-disclosure schedule that shrinks Red's rotation shadow to one quarter — but only on the coalition book. Vendor bought peace everywhere it was bleeding: settlement with NationalCo, an AG assurance, a hard spin that split the conflicted franchise into two sellable stories at a marked-down multiple, and Summit's conversion to SaaS that quietly made Vendor the substrate under Blue's own utility. The unresolved fact of the endgame: adverse actions did not disappear, they changed clothes. Pricing enforcement and financial-accuracy recovery open a fresh two-turn shadow on every book v1.1 does not cover, and Blue's medical-necessity-trained engines are mistargeted against it exactly as D3 predicts. Final standings on own-book economics: Green first, decisively; Red second, holding PMPM, Stars, and retention while surrendering yield mix; Blue third, winning cost and margin conditions but only a small cumulative leakage decline from the 2026 baseline; Vendor fourth — ARR intact, conflict flag downgraded not cleared, multiple compressed.
env: REGULATORY (W1 guaranteed): Two more player-relevant states operationalized HITL audit regimes (four of six now live; roughly a dozen nationally), and CMS issued sub-regulatory guidance requiring plan-level public reporting of prior-auth turnaround AND appeal-overturn rates by service category — data that immediately feeds patient-AI tools, Green RFPs, and Lakeview-style data-qualified gold-card triggers.

COURTS (W1 roll: ruling occurred): The Lokken-line court granted class certification on the surviving contract/good-faith theories and, under W1 settlement speed, approved a process-term settlement within the turn — clinician-determination attestation, override logging, external-review referral, and batch re-review of legacy denial inventory. GovProgramCo's pre-filed compact was cited from the bench as an adequate remedial benchmark, validating its arbitrage.

MEDIA (W1 guaranteed, anti-payer bias): The rural series closed its arc on 'the denial moved into the price' — a final installment documenting site-of-service downgrades and contract-pricing recoupments replacing medical-necessity denials, naming RegionalMutual's turn-open notices. Prairie's untouched fast-pay terms blunted the sharpest frame. The Cleave spin drew one-cycle coverage as 'the two-sided vendor forced to choose.'

EMPLOYERS (W1 response): One non-table jumbo executed a direct-contract carve-out effective 1/1/2030 using Green's replication kit; a second demanded the v1.1 vector-transparency schedule from its incumbent carrier in its 2030 RFP — the schedule's first movement beyond the coalition book.

PATIENT-AI (W1 exogenous doubling): Assisted appeals rose from 8% to 16% of contested adverse determinations, now auto-citing the published CMS turnaround data and the Lokken settlement terms, with success rates at the 80.7% MA base rate on the shrinking clinical-denial pool. White notes the tools have little purchase on provider-facing pricing disputes — the volume follows the old war, not the new one.

FTC/AG (W1 midwifery): The second-state AG executed the assurance of discontinuance with Vendor tied to the completed separation; the supervising AG continued active oversight of the trust and formally endorsed the GovProgramCo compact filings. No new inquiries opened — the enforcement docket is clearing as the parties settle.

LABOR: The NationalCo-Vendor settlement lifted the talent freeze; SIU and edit-library engineers dispersed across the two separated Vendor entities and NationalCo's financial-accuracy build-out. Provider rev-cycle teams began retraining from medical-necessity appeals toward contract-compliance and underpayment analytics — the workforce signature of the vector shift.

resolutions.move: Coalition Appeals Utility (Summit engine as shared service; Prairie exits Vendor MSA)
resolutions.rationale: Service extension of a live at-scale capability, not a new D3 build track — allowed, but rural onboarding friction imposes a two-quarter lag on Prairie integration. Sustained >60% overturns achieved on legacy medical-necessity inventory, and Prairie's swap of 22% contingency for flat fees cuts adverse-action cost. But D3 §1.2/Ex.1 governs the forward fight: Red evacuated the contested vectors same-turn, so flip-condition (a) fired on terrain Red had already priced as ROI-negative; against the new pricing-enforcement vector the engine deploys mistargeted, effectiveness halved pending a one-turn re-instrumentation that runs past the horizon.

resolutions.move: Downcode Counter-Battery — auditor-armed clawback plus Lokken push to merits
resolutions.rationale: Both D3 §4 flip conditions the move targeted literally fired on Red's own ledger: the downcode vector went clawback-negative (NationalCo exited it) and litigation-past-discovery plus six enacted statutes priced continued algorithmic clinical denial above 2x yield (W1 court speed delivered class certification and fast process-term settlements, including legacy-inventory batch re-review). Credit is docked in narrative only: NationalCo's self-report captured the story, so Blue got the money and the process terms but not the scandal.

Partial because Red granted these terms over vectors it was abandoning; the simultaneous rotation into contract-pricing enforcement sits outside every rider Lakeview signed and opens a fresh shadow on its book per D3 §1.2.

resolutions.move: NationalCo Preemptive Clawback Cure and Financial-Accuracy Rotation
resolutions.rationale: D3 §1.2 gives the rotation same-turn effect with a 2-turn unobserved shadow on non-coalition and fully-insured books; on the coalition book Green's v1.1 disclosure schedule compresses the shadow to one quarter — a contract term, not a Blue capability build, so D3 measurement-lag physics do not shield Red there. cellAssessments.blue: Third on own-book economics despite winning nearly every instrument fight it picked. Blue's asymmetric-patience doctrine was vindicated on paper tracks — litigation (Lokken class cert and process-term settlement), statutes (six HITL states via its evidence packages), and the employer channel (direct contract live Jan 2028, tranche two, first external jumbo) all matured on D3 clocks. But both capability builds died on dice: the Meridian telemetry pilot suffered two consecutive stalls (d20=3, then d20=1 with every modifier banked) and was dead by 2028, leaving Blue permanently blind to un-noticed rotation. Blue harvested the war it instrumented for — medical-necessity denial — and ended the game with engines mistargeted against Red's pricing/financial-accuracy destination. Small cumulative leakage decline from the 2026 baseline; strategic position for 2031 is weak outside coalition paper.
cellAssessments.red: Second, and arguably the doctrinally cleanest play on the board. Red read its own ledger every turn: it conceded only terrain that was already ROI-negative (rural pre-pay edits, >70%-overturn MA categories), dressed each retreat as goodwill (Fast-Pay Guarantee bent the media arc; PA eliminations banked Stars protection), and paid in paper — never economics — to hold the ASO book (Standard v1 acceptance, guaranteed-outcome renewals, the direct-network wrapper that co-opts employer defection). The costly error was signing sponsor-selected auditors onto the coalition book one turn before running a downcode surge across it, forcing the T3 self-report and clawback cure. The endgame evacuation into COB/eligibility/subrogation/contract-pricing/site-of-service — outside HITL scope, appeal-proof, clawback-resistant — preserved yield mix at the cost of surrendering the clinical-denial channel entirely. GovProgramCo's Stars-sunset arbitrage under the AG's own consent-decree template was the quietest, most efficient value capture in the game.
cellAssessments.green: Decisive winner — the only cell paid in every direction at once: clawback dollars and auditor top-ups from NationalCo, restitution-as-credits and a monitor from RegionalMutual, both carriers on Standard v1 (piloted threshold met), a published audited comparator that armed every future renewal, and the v1.1 vector-disclosure schedule that shrank Red's rotation shadow to one quarter on coalition paper. Green's side-neutrality was load-bearing: it rewarded NationalCo with retention when the clawback paid, punished RegionalMutual until it signed, fired Vendor on the failed cure, and kept Blue partners only while the comparator held. Green solved the game's central problem — rotation detection — by contract, after Blue failed to solve it by analytics. Its limit is scope: everything it built binds the coalition book only; the rest of the market inherits nothing automatically.
cellAssessments.vendor: Fourth: commercial winner of Turn 1, structural loser of the game. The dual-sided arbitrage model printed ARR exactly as designed — contingency take-rates compounding with conflict intensity, sword to GovProgramCo, shield to Green — and simultaneously manufactured the board's most potent liabilities: parallel firewall attestations, a hedged conflict certification that triggered Green's void-and-disgorgement remedy, and Rotation Radar, which surfaced on a public docket through the very TRO fight Vendor's settlement gambit failed to avert. The T3 pivot to monetizing resolution (Cleave spin, AG assurance, NationalCo global settlement with certified Radar destruction, SaaS conversion) salvaged the franchise at a marked-down multiple — and left Vendor, ironically, as the substrate under Blue's own appeals utility. Conflict flag downgraded, not cleared.
