rapporteur.endStateFreeDescription: By end-2030 the war over clinical denial is finished — not because either side won it, but because the payer side evacuated the terrain once its own ledger showed the vector was the worst-priced asset it held. Six human-in-the-loop statutes (four with operating audit regimes), a class-certified algorithmic-denial settlement with batch re-review, patient-AI at 16% of contested determinations converging on the 80.7% overturn base rate, and finality-based fee clawbacks had jointly repriced medical-necessity denial to unprofitability. Red's response was neither detente nor exhaustion: it rotated its recovery engines wholesale into financial-accuracy and pricing enforcement — COB, eligibility, subrogation, duplicate payment, contract-pricing compliance, site-of-service — vectors that survive appeal, escape every clawback, and sit outside the statutes' medical-necessity scope. Adverse actions did not decline; they changed clothes. The abandoned terrain is fenced with genuinely binding paper: gold cards, notice floors, transparency schedules, process-term settlements — all real, all cheap for Red to grant because they fence what it no longer wants. The purchaser coalition holds the only functioning detection instrument in the new war — a contractual quarterly vector-disclosure schedule with fee-finality objection windows — but only on coalition paper; every non-coalition book enters 2031 inside a fresh two-turn rotation shadow. Blue's medical-necessity-trained appeal engines are mistargeted against pricing disputes, its analytics builds are dead, and patient-AI tools have no purchase on provider-facing pricing fights. The equilibrium is a displaced, re-instrumenting conflict: high transparency and heavy process obligations on the old battlefield, open shadow on the new one, with employers — not regulators — holding the binding leash on self-funded volume, and the first contested cycle of the pricing war scheduled for 2031.
rapporteur.excursionSummary: Game B3G2 ran doctrine D3 (asymmetric friction physics: payer capability lands same-turn, provider builds run multi-turn clocks with stall/death dice) in world W1 (activist regulator, fast courts, anti-payer media) from a seed of consolidated payers pressing automated adjudication into an under-resourced provider tier. The game's arc is a three-act displacement. Act one: Red harvested uncontested yield in the shadow while Blue lit every slow fuse — litigation, statutes, data trust, employer channel — and the environment turned activist underneath Red (six HITL statutes, compelled algorithm production, a rural-hospitals media series). Act two: the dice killed Blue's measurement layer (telemetry pilot death after consecutive stalls) and pried Lakeview out of the trust, while Blue's paper tracks all advanced: direct contract live January 2028, Summit's appeals engine at enterprise scale above the 60% flip threshold, Lokken production feeding two state audits. Red, reading its own P&L, exited burned vectors behind a Fast-Pay Guarantee and — decisively — signed Green's Contract Standard v1 with clawback to hold the coalition book, installing the auditors that would document its own downcode rotation. Act three: everything matured at once. Blue harvested class certification, process-term settlements, gold-card expansions, and a favorable audited comparator year; Green got paid in every direction — clawbacks, restitution, a second carrier on the Standard, and a v1.1 vector-disclosure schedule that achieved by contract the rotation detection Blue failed to build by analytics; Vendor bought peace at a compressed multiple after Rotation Radar surfaced in discovery; and Red evacuated clinical denial entirely, swinging into COB, subrogation, eligibility, and contract-pricing recovery that no statute, appeal engine, or patient-AI tool on the board can reach. Final standings on own-book economics: Green first decisively, Red second, Blue third, Vendor fourth. The load-bearing findings: yield displaced rather than disappeared under every constraint; process terms signed everywhere while the anti-rotation clause sat unsigned for three turns (no Red ledger ever priced rotation coverage below rotation); every Red de-escalation was proximately triggered by litigation, regulation, media, or employer abrasion — never cumulative cost; the employer channel, not the activist regulator, bound Red's self-funded PI behavior first, because statutes reach medical necessity while ASO economics reach everything; and dual-sided vendor arbitrage printed ARR while manufacturing the discoverable artifacts that destroyed its exit multiple. The game ends with a new contest opened and unscored: pricing enforcement on non-coalition books, against which the winning side's instruments are mistargeted.
keyDynamics: Yield displacement under constraint: every binding limit on denial (statutes, clawbacks, overturn economics) produced rotation into adjacent adverse-action channels — downcodes in 2028, then COB/eligibility/subrogation/contract-pricing/site-of-service by 2030 — rather than net reduction; the closing media frame was 'the denial moved into the price.'

Detection asymmetry as the true contest: D3's rotation shadow, not denial volume, drove strategy. Blue's analytic detection died twice on dice; detection was ultimately achieved by contract — 60-90 day notice floors, sponsor-selected auditors with claim-line access, and Green's v1.1 quarterly vector-disclosure schedule — and only on the books those contracts cover.

The purchaser channel outran the activist regulator on self-funded volume: statutes and audits reached medical-necessity UM, but the terms that actually changed Red's ASO behavior were Green's award auction, finality-based fee clawbacks, and auditor access — because the retention index priced higher than any PI fee stream.

Process terms sign; outcome terms never do: fourteen-plus process/fee/transparency instruments bound and sustained, while the Anti-Rotation Scope Clause — ruled signable — sat unsigned three consecutive turns because no Red ledger ever priced rotation coverage below rotation.

Ledger-driven concession theater: Red's most applauded retreats (Fast-Pay Guarantee, MA PA eliminations, gold-card expansions) were exits from vectors its own P&L already showed as ROI-negative, converting inevitable evacuations into PR, Stars protection, and cheap contract currency.

Dual-sided vendor arbitrage is self-poisoning: conflict monetization compounded ARR and simultaneously generated the game's most potent discoverable artifacts (parallel firewall attestations, hedged certifications, Rotation Radar), forcing structural separation at a marked-down multiple.

Exogenous compounding of patient-AI (2%→4%→8%→16%, statute-citing, converging on the 80.7% overturn base rate) steadily repriced clinical denial — but has no purchase on provider-facing pricing disputes, so the volume follows the old war, not the new one.

registryScores.evidence: Displacement observed unambiguously and repeatedly in this D3xW1 game: when HITL statutes, clawbacks, and overturn economics constrained clinical denial, NationalCo rotated into ASO coding-accuracy/downcode recovery within one turn (T2), and when the clawback/auditor regime constrained that, into COB/eligibility/subrogation/duplicate-payment/contract-pricing recovery (T3); RegionalMutual filed turn-open notices rotating into site-of-service and contract-pricing enforcement immediately upon settling. White's closing adjudication ('adverse actions did not disappear, they changed clothes') is a direct statement of the mechanism. However, the record publishes no dollar-denominated adverse-action mix, so the 0.33 displacement ratio cannot be computed, and the invariance claim across 9 cells cannot be tested from one game. Strong qualitative support in-cell; ratio and invariance untested.

The W1 channel-and-lag prediction held for conflict artifacts: Rotation Radar surfaced via expedited discovery within one turn of creation and was weaponized through media re-ignition and a second-state AG inquiry; parallel firewall attestations and the hedged Green certification were logged discoverable at signing and fired Green's void-and-disgorgement remedy a turn later; NationalCo's signed Standard v1 became the vehicle documenting its own downcode surge within a turn. But the rider that no world leaves >=50% of published artifacts cost-free is contradicted in-game: GovProgramCo's published HITL compact was decisively net-positive (cited from the bench as adequate relief, circulated as AG template), the published direct-contract comparator armed its publishers, and the Fast-Pay Guarantee bought Red the media arc. Boomerang confirmed for adversarial-conflict artifacts; publisher-net-negative-majority not confirmed.

No per-turn Blue cost ledger or cost-per-denial figures appear anywhere in this game's record; the White Cell published only qualitative state variables (blueAdverseActionCost: worsening_small → improving_small). Directionally consistent color exists — recurring tolls (trust management, litigation, audits, monitors, arbitration-free but attestation-heavy compliance) persisted even as clinical denial volume collapsed, and Blue's adverse-action cost worsened while denial constraints tightened — but neither the $65/$80 floor nor the volume-down/cost-up correlation can be computed from this record.

Every Red de-escalation in the game carries an adjudicated external trigger, never cumulative cost: the rural pre-pay exit was triggered by the media series plus statute exposure (T2, executed behind the Fast-Pay Guarantee); MA category drains and PA eliminations by Stars-measure timing and patient-AI/CTM pricing; Standard v1 acceptance by the award auction and re-bid threat (employer channel); RegionalMutual's book-wide signing by its position as un-stayed fiduciary defendant with a lost coalition tranche and a 0057-F corrective notice — White explicitly records 'not from goodwill.' Red's PI fee engine stayed positive throughout (redPIYield improving through T2, only worsening_small at end after voluntary yield-mix surrender), and Red finished second on own-book economics. No mutual-pain off-ramp ever appeared; the off-ramps were litigation pricing, regulation, media, and employer abrasion, exactly as the corrected claim predicts.

This D3xW1 game produced no detente-shaped end-state — White's closing line is 'the contest ended by evacuation rather than armistice' — consistent with the claim that broad-detente convergence was a D1 artifact. The instrument record is a clean sweep for the process-term half: every signed-and-sustained instrument is process/fee/transparency paper (notice floors, gold-card criteria, audit rights, disclosure schedules, clawback-as-fee-condition), zero numeric denial-rate corridors were ever signed or even ruled on as proposed, and the checklist-item-1 note (threshold triggers process relief, never a duty to approve N%) shows corridor content was structurally excluded. One game cannot establish the <33% F2 rate across six D2/D3 cells, but as a single D3 draw it lands exactly where the hypothesis predicts on both prongs.

The discriminating paired comparison (publishers vs internal-governors on SIU-audit/qui-tam event rates) cannot be run: no qui tam events occurred and no actor ran the internal-governance-with-gated-publication control. The one charter-like publication — GovProgramCo's HITL clinician-pod protocol and multi-state compact — was strongly net-positive in this W1 game (AG circulated it as consent-decree template; the Lokken bench cited it as adequate remedial benchmark, mooting separate relief), which is consistent with the hypothesis's W1-exception branch (publication pays where a safe-harbor-equivalent exists to enter), though no lookback/extrapolation caps were coded. Weak directional support for the W1 branch; the 2x adverse-event core claim untested.

Leaning against, in this cell: zero distress events of any tier occurred. Lakeview — the closest mid-tier analogue, capital-constrained with 45% single-payer concentration — was squeezed exactly through the predicted mechanism (renewal leverage forced its trust defection at T2) but ended the game with improved terms (expanded gold cards, fast-pay parity, direct-network participation), not distress sale, delegation capture, or PE acquisition. Rural restraint held precisely as predicted: Prairie was shielded by the media cycle, network position, and fast-pay terms throughout — Red's own ledger made rural aggression ROI-negative under W1. So the rural half of the hypothesis is supported and the mid-tier-casualty half produced no confirming event; one W1 game with maximal media/regulatory protection is a weak draw for testing distress, hence partial rather than refuted.

Binding instruments distributed across all three turns with no synchronized window: 2026-27 (Lakeview process riders, gold card, converted master terms), 2028 (NationalCo Standard v1, direct-contract definitive agreements, Prairie gold card), 2029-30 (RegionalMutual Standard acceptance, v1.1 schedule, Lakeview Renewal 2.0, process-term settlements) — no single year approaches a 40% cluster. First-cycle wins were emphatically wedge provisions: named-vector gold cards, notice floors, transparency riders — White twice notes on the record that coverage is named-vector only and rotation elsewhere is unconstrained; full-economics packages never bound in cycle one anywhere. The D2 late-escalation-peak rider is untestable in this D3 game (escalation here plateaued elevated T1-T2 and eased to moderate at T3). Both testable prongs supported.

The hypothesis is defined entirely over D2xW2 and D2xW3 end-state frequencies against a D1xW1 baseline; this is a D3xW1 game and contributes to neither arm of the comparison. For the record, the realized end-state was not grinding uncoordinated escalation — escalation closed at 'moderate' with the conflict displaced into a new vector rather than ground on — but a D3 draw carries no evidentiary weight for the D2 doctrine-ablation question.

Single-cell payoff observations only; the 7-of-9-cells portability claim is untestable here. Within D3xW1: renewal loading paid clearly (Lakeview's process riders compounded into Renewal 2.0 structural terms); BATNA-first paid decisively (direct contract → comparator → tranche two → external adopter); upcoding-inoculation-adjacent hygiene paid for Red (clinician signatures, no-quota paper trail survived discovery). Prevention-over-appeals returned a split verdict: the prevention/telemetry build died on dice while industrialized appeals were Blue's most effective operational lever — an inversion worth flagging for the strategy table. On the fragile side, symmetric escalation was declined by Blue and weak-BATNA anchoring was avoided rather than tested. No fragile strategy was demonstrated winning; no robust strategy went materially negative, but prevention-over-appeals underperformed appeals in this D3 draw.

This is the W1 contrast cell, where the hypothesis predicts the activist regulator should outrun employers — and it did not, on self-funded volume. The first events that measurably curtailed Red PI behavior on the ASO book were employer-channel: the T2 award auction with pre-committed anchor defection forced NationalCo's Standard v1 acceptance (clawback included), and sponsor-selected auditors forced the T3 downcode self-report and cure — while the HITL statutes and audits bound medical-necessity UM but never reached ASO financial-accuracy vectors at all. Contagion also ran through RFPs (two non-table jumbos importing Standard clauses by T2, a third demanding the v1.1 schedule by T3) faster than any statute diffused. This exceeds the hypothesis's expectation for W1, supporting the mechanism strongly — but the specified W2/W3 confirm criteria and the GREEN-inactive control are absent, so the verdict cannot exceed partial.

The behavioral signature is present and adjudicated: Vendor explicitly re-armed the weak side (zero-upfront contingency denial-defense in the undefended tier) while selling PI to Red, structured revenue to compound with conflict intensity, and lobbied to 'keep the dispute pool deep' (anti-corridor lobbying, regulatory moat) — resisting exactly the prevention/touchless terms the hypothesis names. But both discriminating tests are unavailable: no VENDOR-inactive control run of the same seed exists for the duration/term-adoption comparison, and the scripted payer-acquisition-of-provider-vendor inject never fired (the analogous event was NationalCo suing, then settling with, Vendor — with certified Rotation Radar destruction — not acquiring it). Mechanism visible; effect size and the data-rights-screen test unmeasured.

No preemption seed fired and none could: this is a W1 activist-regulator world in which the state channel strengthened every turn (six statutes to four operational audit regimes). The game incidentally demonstrates the F3 rail carrying real load — statutes and audits priced Red's clinical-denial exit — but provides no evidence about what happens when that rail is removed.

No acquisition moves were priced, enabled, or attempted in this cell, so the acquisition-enabled vs disabled comparison cannot run. Noteworthy negative color: facing a fully constrained denial channel, Red's realized responses were vector rotation (financial-accuracy, pricing enforcement) and co-option via the direct-network administration wrapper — converting employer defection into carrier-administered carve-outs — rather than any move toward owning provider assets; and classic F4-via-VBC stayed marginal (one provisional post-acute risk-transfer repricing at GovProgramCo). Consistent with integration not being the default constrained-channel response when rotation remains cheap, but the hypothesis's own conditions were not present.

The floor held emphatically in a D3 cell: multiple instruments from the payer-signable set bound and sustained to end-game — 60-90 day change-notice floors (T1 conversion, still operative and upgraded to 90-day flat with mid-cycle disclosure at T3), gold-card entry criteria (Lakeview T1, Prairie T2, expanded schedules T3), audit rights and edit-disclosure/transparency reporting (process riders, Standard v1/v1.1 quarterly vector reporting), and model/policy-change disclosure via the notice regime. Every one survived multiple turns; several compounded. One game cannot establish the >=60%-of-games floor in all 9 cells, but as a draw from an asymmetric-friction doctrine it is a clean positive: even a payer refusing all rotation-covering paper for three consecutive turns signed and honored the entire process-term set.

surprises: Green, not Blue, solved the game's central technical problem: rotation detection was achieved by contract (v1.1 vector-disclosure with fee-finality objection windows) after Blue's two analytics builds died on dice — the shadow was closed by paper, not telemetry, and only on the coalition book.

The boomerang ran backwards for GovProgramCo: publishing its HITL compliance compact — the most charter-like artifact in the game — was decisively net-positive, cited from the bench as adequate relief and circulated by the AG as a template, converting regulatory exposure into an audit-proof shield for continued MA discipline.

Red's most celebrated concessions were free: the Fast-Pay Guarantee and MA PA eliminations exited vectors Red's own ledger already showed as ROI-negative, meaning W1's anti-payer media pressure was 'satisfied' at near-zero economic cost while the yield engine rotated intact.

The Vendor settlement's certified Rotation Radar destruction extinguished the board's single most potent discoverable artifact — an adversary's litigation win (NationalCo's) ended up laundering the whole board's shared evidence trail.

Lakeview, the actor with the weakest hand (45% single-payer concentration), ended the game better off than coalition loyalty would have delivered: its trust defection cost Blue the notice feed but its banked process riders compounded into the strongest bilateral renewal terms on the board — defection paid.

The endgame contains neither of the two canonical closures — no detente instrument and no exhaustion spiral. The conflict was conserved and re-vectored: Blue 'won' the medical-necessity war on points at the exact moment the war stopped being about medical necessity, and the scoring horizon closed with a fresh two-turn shadow already open on every non-coalition book.

Patient-AI, the fastest-compounding force in the game (2% to 16%), was revealed at endgame as strategically inert against the new battlefield — White notes the tools 'follow the old war, not the new one' — a rare case of an exponential trend being neutralized by vector migration rather than countermeasures.

frictionViolations.rule: §3.2 — IT/AI deployments take 12–24 months to measurable impact
frictionViolations.violation: NationalCo's pre-pay yield engine 'activated inside the turn' and banked measurable edit/downcode yield same-turn, justified by a cited doctrine that 'D3 grants payer capability plays same-turn effect.' The provided friction text contains no payer carve-out; the same turn, Blue's telemetry build was subjected to multi-turn clocks and stall rolls. Mitigation: NationalCo is chartered as already-frontier automation (extension, not build), the base-rate table (§6) documents payers 2–3 yrs ahead of providers, and the ~18-month turn length means a 12-month clock can fit inside one turn.

frictionViolations.rule: §3.2 / clock accounting — build and channel gates denominated consistently
frictionViolations.violation: Clock notations are in 6-month units ('T+3-4 employer-channel gate,' 'clock paused 2 D3-turns,' 'base 5 D3-turns') while the game's actual turns run ~18–20 months. The Green direct-contract gate declared 'T+3-4' at Turn 1 was ruled satisfied at Turn 2 (Jan 2028) — correct if units are 6-month periods, a 2–3x acceleration if units are game turns. The record never states which denominator governs; gate satisfaction is therefore unauditable as written.

frictionViolations.rule: §3.3 — bounded movement: denial rates ±2 pts per turn absent a White-declared structural break
frictionViolations.violation: GovProgramCo 'drained every MA denial category running above 70% overturn' within the turn, an unquantified category-level elimination that plausibly exceeds a 2-pt denial-rate move; no structural break was declared for it. Mitigating: the movement is a denial reduction (payer's own retreat), and high-overturn denials were mostly being reversed anyway, limiting net effect.

frictionViolations.rule: §3.2 — contract terms bind only at renewal
frictionViolations.violation: NationalCo's Rural Fast-Pay Guarantee was executed as mid-cycle contract amendments 'in force same-turn per D3 payer clocks.' Low distortion — a unilateral concession requires no renewal leverage and mutual mid-cycle amendment is legally ordinary — but the record again invokes an asymmetric 'payer clock' not present in the provided friction rules.

frictionViolations.rule: §3.2 — IT/AI deployments take 12–24 months to measurable impact
frictionViolations.violation: NationalCo 'swung its engine' into COB/eligibility/subrogation/duplicate-payment recovery and RegionalMutual filed turn-open notices rotating into site-of-service/contract-pricing enforcement, all inside the scoring turn. Retargeting PI analytics to new vector classes is a build. Substantially mitigated: the record scored redPIYield 'worsening_small' at T3 and deferred the rotation's yield to a post-game 'first contested cycle 2031' — the effect was mostly NOT credited within the horizon.

baseRateViolations.expected: World-model common rules: 1 turn = ~6 months, 8–10 turns over 2026–2030
baseRateViolations.observed: Game ran 3 turns of ~18–20 months each (2026-27, 2028, 2029-30). Note the source documents conflict internally — D3 §3.1 references an '18-month turn' — but W1's quantitative calibrations (doubling per turn, by-T4/by-T6 milestones, 1–2 employers per turn) were written for 6-month turns and were applied per long turn without rescaling, systematically slowing the assigned activist environment. Fewer turns also means each stall/defection die roll carries 2–3x the intended weight.

baseRateViolations.expected: W1: appeal-bot adoption doubles per 6-month turn from 2% base; 25–35% of adverse determinations contested with AI assistance by T6 (~2029)
baseRateViolations.observed: 2% → 4% → 8% → 16% at end-2030 — literal per-turn doubling applied to 18-month turns, ending materially below the assigned W1 trajectory. Deviation is in the conservative direction (environment weaker than spec, not stronger).

baseRateViolations.expected: W1: 15+ states with live AI-UR regimes by T4 (~2028); operational enforcement 1–2 turns behind passage
baseRateViolations.observed: Six player-relevant states passed at T1, only 4 of 6 operational by T3, 'roughly a dozen nationally' by 2029-30. Undershoots the assigned activist spec's breadth and timing; same turn-compression root cause. Conservative direction.

baseRateViolations.expected: Litigation clock: filing → settlement years 4–7; W1 accelerates denial/AI-UR suits but the Green ERISA fiduciary action is adjacent, not squarely covered
baseRateViolations.observed: Green fiduciary action filed T2 (2028), resolved T3 (2029-30) with fee restitution and a two-year monitor — ~1.5–2 years filing-to-settlement. Partly legitimate (defendant voluntarily settled to win the book, and the record had earlier flagged the suit as 'scored immature absent early settlement'), but it is the fastest clock in the record relative to its base rate.

audit.worldModelFidelity: Qualitatively high fidelity to W1-ACTIVIST: every event-frequency floor was met (guaranteed regulatory action all 3 turns; court process-term rulings 2 of 3 turns vs the 1-in-2 spec; a media event every turn with anti-payer amplification and a 2-3-turn payer-scandal arc); CMS enforced 0057-F strictly at Jan 2027 with zero extensions and corrective-action notices exactly as the W1 example update prescribes; FTC/AG midwifery appeared repeatedly (active-supervision pre-clearance for the data trust, consent-decree template circulation, assurance of discontinuance); employers responded to scandals at 1-2 jumbos per turn; patient-AI doubled each turn and cited statutes; class certification and fast process-term settlements matched W1 court posture. The record also honored the base-rate table where W1 does not override it — diffusion rulings repeatedly denied stage advances against the CAQH/Da Vinci/15-year-standards anchors, gold cards stayed named-vector per HB 3459, 0057-F real interop was held to the 2-3-years-post-deadline lag, and Lokken behavioral change arrived at the discovery stage per the litigation clock. The one structural infidelity is quantitative: the game compressed 8-10 six-month turns into 3 turns of ~18-20 months (arguably licensed by D3 §3.1's own '18-month turn' language, an internal contradiction in the source documents) and applied W1's per-turn rates per long turn, so the environment under-delivered the assigned activist intensity — 16% patient-AI at end-2030 vs the 25-35%-by-2029 spec, ~a dozen statute states by 2029-30 vs 15+ by 2028. The deviation runs in the conservative direction: the realized world sat between W1 and the W2 null world, meaning pro-oversight forcing functions were understated, not overstated.
downweightRecommendations: Down-weight the finding that Blue analytics/telemetry capability cannot mature within the horizon and that rotation detection must be solved by contract rather than instrumentation: it rests on two consecutive failed stall rolls under a two-stalls-equals-death mechanic in a game with only ~3 milestone opportunities total. In the specified 8-10-turn structure, a restarted pilot could have matured. Treat this as one unlucky draw, not a distribution — the contractual-detection result (v1.1 disclosure schedule) is a valid path, but 'analytics is dead' is mechanics-driven.

Down-weight magnitude claims about patient-AI's limited end-state role (16% contest share, 'little purchase on the new war'): the realized adoption curve ran materially below the assigned W1 spec due to turn compression. Under spec-faithful W1 (25-35% by 2029), the clinical-denial evacuation would have been forced earlier and harder, and bot-originated statutory claims under private rights of action would likely have appeared within the horizon.

Down-weight the breadth/ceiling of regulatory pressure conclusions (e.g., 'four of six states operational,' penalties absent by game end): statute-state counts and operationalization ran below the assigned activist spec. Findings that regulatory enforcement bite arrives late even in a favorable world partly reflect the compressed turn structure, not W1 as specified.

Discount Red's Turn-1 first-mover yield advantage by one notch: the same-turn payer-capability clock ('D3 grants payer capability plays same-turn effect') has no basis in the provided friction rules and was applied asymmetrically against Blue's build clocks. The direction is defensible (base-rate §6: payers lead by 2-3 years) but the size of the T1 harvest and the 'Red always rotates inside Blue's OODA loop' conclusion is partially rule-granted rather than played out.

Retain at full weight: the Green result (sponsor-selected auditors + finality-based clawbacks + vector-disclosure schedules as the highest-leverage instruments) — it was achieved through renewal-cycle-compliant paper and survived W1-independent mechanics; the 'adverse actions change clothes' rotation endgame into financial-accuracy/pricing enforcement — base-rate consistent and correctly left unresolved; and all diffusion-ledger conclusions (coalition-infrastructure-not-industry-infrastructure, infrastructure-by-capture denied), which were adjudicated hard against the base-rate table.

Because the realized environment undershot W1, do NOT read this game as evidence that even an activist world leaves Blue third and litigation/statutes under-powered by 2030 — that conclusion needs a rerun at spec-faithful W1 intensity or 8-10 true turns before it generalizes.

games.name: Detente Corridor
games.seed: Blue (led by Meridian and Lakeview) opens with a negotiated posture: proposes SIGNABLE process instruments per the legal checklist (machine-readable edit-library disclosure, 60-90 day change notice, audit rights, gold-card entry criteria). RegionalMutual is receptive; NationalCo is skeptical and keeps arming; GovProgramCo is margin-constrained. Green is watching for terms it can import into ASO RFPs. Vendor sees corridor instruments as a threat to disputed-dollar volume.

turns.narrative: The opening period rewarded tempo and punished anyone waiting for the environment to behave. NationalCo executed the cleanest play on the board: a quiet shift of its ASO payment-integrity engine from front-end edits into pre-pay clinical validation and DRG review, timed behind a loud, cheap prior-auth retreat concentrated in code families that were approved 95%+ of the time anyway. Because Meridian's denial-vector telemetry only came online late in the turn, most of that rotation ran unobserved — Red banked fee yield on employer money exactly as D3 physics allow. GovProgramCo, betting early on CMS-0057-F compliance, looked prescient when CMS spent the year contradicting itself, and its relocation of MA friction from member-visible prior auth into provider-facing post-pay audit protected the Stars measures that still bite through 2028. RegionalMutual, squeezed between home-market optics, a visibly shopping jumbo employer, and a leaked vendor sales deck, signed the turn's only bilateral instrument: gold-carding in imaging and cardiology, 60-day edit-change notice in covered categories, and — the real concession, extracted after White converted Blue's rotation-notice demand into reporting-and-trigger form — quarterly adverse-action mix reporting across all vectors. Blue got less than it wanted and more than base rates predicted. Its coalition utility survived declaration with telemetry live and appeals automation in limited production after a talent-raid stall, but an FTC civil investigative demand into the shared-services structure — landing the same week a payer services acquisition cleared with light conditions — froze Prairie and Summit's subscriptions, and Prairie promptly hedged into both RegionalMutual's PA concierge and the Vendor's contingency appeals service. Meridian's suit against NationalCo survived its first screen only in part, with counter-discovery now aimed at Meridian's own documentation AI, and one target state's new AI-UR statute sits frozen under a circulating federal preemption order. Green was the quiet winner of positioning: its Procurement Standard is in the 1/1/2028 RFP stream, its CAA record is built, and its conflict-disclosure requirement forced the Vendor into the turn's defining embarrassment — a partial disclosure judged insufficient, disqualification from the anchor audit, and public circulation of the refusal just as the "rotation-as-a-feature" deck leaked to the trade press. The Vendor still grew — GovProgramCo signed contingency modules, Prairie signed Denial Shield — but its both-sides model is now a documented fact sitting in a Blue contract rep, a Green procurement file, and a reporter's inbox. Nothing structural matured this turn; every clock that matters is now running, and the mandatory W3 shock still waits offstage.
env: MEDIA (W3 mandatory hostile story; randomized target landed on Vendor/Red): A leaked Vendor sales deck marketing 'quarterly denial-vector retargeting' to payer clients — while the same holding company sells appeals automation to providers — runs in trade press and crosses into national coverage as 'the firm that sells the disease and the cure.' Green benefits consultants circulate it to every jumbo account; RegionalMutual publicly declines the rotation feature.

ANTITRUST ASYMMETRY (W3 1-in-3 roll on provider coordination — HIT): FTC issues a civil investigative demand into the Blue coalition's shared denial-defense utility and pooled anonymized denial dataset as potential buyer-side coordination among competing providers; the same week, a payer services-arm acquisition clears review with light conditions. Prairie and Summit pause subscription signatures; coalition counsel restructures the data pool toward independent-manager form.

CMS (W3 posture roll: silent/contradictory): A mid-year CMS FAQ suggests 'good-faith attestation' flexibility on CMS-0057-F API readiness; a subsequent bulletin reasserts full January 2027 enforcement with penalty exposure. Compliance planning whipsaws industry-wide; early builders (GovProgramCo) are hedged, late starters freeze spend awaiting clarity.

FEDERAL PREEMPTION (W3 statute rule, 1-in-3 per regime — one HIT): A draft executive order asserting federal preemption of state AI-regulation regimes circulates; one player-relevant state that enacted an SB 1120-copy AI-UR statute stays its operationalization pending review. Other statehouses slow their floor calendars; Blue's legislative-track value is discounted accordingly.

PATIENT-AI: Appeal-bot usage grows from the ~2% base toward high single digits of contested adverse determinations, concentrated in commercial and MA populations and amplified by denial-story coverage — volatile trajectory; the W3 mandatory trust shock remains ahead (T2-T3 window), after which adoption craters then returns litigation-oriented.

sign.instrument: BLUE: Machine-readable adverse-action policy-library disclosure + 75-day change notice drafted to cover vector rotation
sign.detail: Disclosure and policy-change notice are signable as-is (checklist items 6-7). The rotation-coverage clause is not: an obligation to give advance notice of any shift in adverse-action MIX is notice of outcomes rather than policy changes and functions as a constraint on UM output. Converted per checklist item 1 to reporting-and-trigger form: quarterly retrospective adverse-action mix reporting by vector (edits/pends/downcodes/eligibility) with breach-of-threshold triggering audit rights and joint review — never a duty to hold any rate.

sign.instrument: BLUE: Bilateral audit rights with escalation SLAs and named-clinician peer review (SB 1120-conformant)
sign.detail: Ordinary contract terms mirroring CMS downstream-audit norms and live state AI-UM statutes; signed into the RegionalMutual compact.

sign.instrument: BLUE: Objective gold-card entry/exit criteria with continuity-of-care protections
sign.detail: Statutorily blessed model (Tex. Ins. Code ch. 4201 subch. N); contractual gold-carding can exceed statute. Signed for imaging/cardiology at 92% trailing approval.

sign.instrument: BLUE: Coalition accession clause (most-favored-coalition extension to Summit/Prairie)
sign.detail: As drafted, competitors jointly obtaining identical negotiated terms edges into checklist item 2 (collective negotiation by non-integrated competitors; no safety zones post-2023 withdrawal) and MFN restrictions in ~20 states. Converted to payer-offered open accession: RegionalMutual unilaterally offers identical process terms to any network provider meeting published criteria at that provider's own renewal.

sign.instrument: BLUE: Vendor conflict-of-interest disclosure representation in Blue-side vendor contracts
sign.detail: Ordinary representation-and-warranty term. Now live in Prairie's Denial Shield contract — the discoverable-fact machinery Blue wanted exists.

sign.instrument: BLUE: CAA-audit data-access rider offered to Green
sign.detail: Signable, with the ERISA §514 caveat enforced: it reaches the self-funded book only as an executed ASO contract term. Imported into Green's Standard v1 as paper this turn; binds no carrier until a 1/1/2028 award.

sign.instrument: RED: Scoped Gold-Card and Change-Notice Rider (RegionalMutual) with standstill + legislative-withdrawal consideration
sign.detail: The process terms are signable. The consideration package is not, as drafted: the clause requiring Blue signatories to withdraw active support for pending state AI-UR legislation is struck as an unenforceable restraint on petitioning (public-policy/Noerr-Pennington territory); the open-ended prospective standstill on UM-algorithm claims is narrowed to a mutual release/covenant limited to covered categories during the 2-year term, RegionalMutual only. Red's own fallback (mutual pre-submission data-exchange) substituted as additional consideration.

sign.instrument: RED: Employer Transparency Rider (NationalCo jumbo ASO accounts)
sign.detail: Disclosure, auditor-panel audit rights, fee-structure election — all commercial terms; no corridor. Signable as-is; White notes the auditor-panel and materiality-threshold design gives NationalCo control of its own audit exposure, a fact Green may contest commercially.

sign.instrument: GREEN: Coalition ASO Procurement Standard v1 (RFP rider)
sign.detail: Audit rights, Sec. 408(b)(2)-style compensation disclosure, contingency-fee caps, clawback of fees on overturned recoveries, plan-level denial-data feeds, AI-UR attestation: all compensation/disclosure/audit terms a CAA fiduciary may demand of its own TPA. Contains no denial-rate corridor or quota. Buyer-coalition purchasing standards for ASO services raise no material monopsony concern at this scale.

sign.instrument: GREEN: Independent PI Audit Engagement Template (flat-fee + sworn affiliate-revenue conflict disclosure)
sign.detail: Ordinary professional-services terms. The sworn both-sides disclosure requirement is enforceable and did its work this turn.

sign.instrument: GREEN: Direct-Contract Term Sheet (bundled episodes / advanced primary care)
sign.detail: Bilateral commercial contract with independent TPA administration; no signability issue. Unsigned as of turn end — status is negotiation, not instrument.

sign.instrument: VENDOR: Edit Transparency Clearinghouse (vendor-hosted, NDA-tiered)
sign.detail: Pooled competitively sensitive payer rule data requires an independent third-party manager with aggregation/de-identification safeguards (checklist item 4). An operator whose affiliate sells edit engines to depositors and appeals automation against those same edits is not independent; the 'information firewall' is cosmetic. Converted to require a genuinely independent operator — which eliminates the Vendor's data-position rationale. Zero adopters this turn.

sign.instrument: VENDOR: Standard ASO Audit-Data Specification (free template to Green)
sign.detail: A data-format template is signable trivially; White records it as an attempted standards capture. The Green coalition declined it after the audit disqualification.

diff.note: Signatory-level benefit only, and economic effect begins at T2 renewals per friction rules. Designed diffusion path is Green importation into ASO RFPs, not organic spread — base rates are hostile (new contract-language class reaches majority of agreements in 10-15 yrs organically, 5-7 yrs if statutorily forced; gold-card statutory uptake ran ~3%). External-adopter threshold White will apply at T2: at least two non-table payers or a state adopting the reporting template.

Fastest plausible path to 'early_external_adopters' is consultant-channel copying during the 2027 RFP season — plausible but unproven; White will require evidence of non-coalition employers issuing the rider.

Live on a subset of jumbo ASO accounts. A unilateral carrier product, not a multilateral standard — it diffuses only as far as NationalCo's book, and its function is defensive (preempting Green's terms of reference).
Converted at the signability gate to require an independent operator; no depositor or subscriber signed. Effectively dead unless restructured under a genuinely neutral entity.
Rejected by the Green coalition after the auditor disqualification; residual chance of uptake among lagging non-coalition employers, which would be capture by default rather than adoption on merits.

Imported into Green Standard v1 as a scored-preference term — Blue's zero-cost diffusion bet paid at the paper stage. Reaches the self-funded book only via executed ASO contracts (ERISA §514), so real coverage waits on T2 awards.
Executed in Prairie's Denial Shield contract. Small instrument, outsized effect: it is the first contractual record of the Vendor's both-sides book and is discoverable in any T2-T3 proceeding.

turns.narrative: The mandatory shock arrived mid-year: a consumer appeals platform was caught mass-producing appeals with fabricated clinician attestations, and days later a UM subcontractor breach spilled utilization records complete with algorithmic denial-score rationales. Congressional hearings aimed at payer algorithms and provider documentation AI alike; health-AI trust polling collapsed and patient-bot appeal volume halved. Every cell had priced this event; none controlled its timing. Against that backdrop the 1/1/2028 renewals executed. RegionalMutual took the anchor employer's regional carve-out and two mid-size accounts as payment for being the transparency carrier; NationalCo held most of its national book by conceding fee elections, overturn clawbacks, and jumbo-account auditor selection — while quietly winning the clause fight that matters: clawbacks trigger on reversals, and its yield now lives in vectors that rarely reverse. NationalCo's second rotation — out of clinical validation into COB, eligibility, subrogation, and itemized-bill technical review — was observed within the quarter by Meridian's live telemetry and contested by nothing, because Meridian spent its re-instrumentation point on the vector NationalCo was vacating. D3's arithmetic held: the appeals engine reached enterprise scale and pushed overturns past 60% on the residual clinical pool, but GovProgramCo's fast-pay protocol drained that pool from the other end, so flip condition (a) receded even as Blue's machinery matured. The compact deepened regardless: Lakeview acceded at renewal and got its DRG/downcode reporting addendum signed — RegionalMutual could afford the signature, having moved trend management to specialty pharmacy, which no instrument at the table touches; a one-cycle oncology white-bagging story flared in its home market and died. Discovery in Meridian v. NationalCo produced PI fee schedules and rotation-timing documents, a slice of them unsealed into the trade press; counter-discovery reached Meridian's documentation AI; the settlement corridor stayed shut because no internal recovery-target document surfaced. The FTC closed its CID after the denial-data pool restructured under a genuinely independent manager — the same month a payer PBM acquisition cleared with no conditions. The preemption executive order was signed and promptly enjoined; the stayed AI-UR statute resumed operationalization into an audit-lagged enforcement pipeline. The Vendor cut itself in two — honestly enough to earn a firewall attestation, not enough to pass Green's certificate, because common HoldCo ownership is still affiliate revenue; the coalition door stays priced at divestiture. Its appeal-provenance specification, published weeks before the scandal broke, was the turn's best-timed product with almost no revenue attached. Summit's and Meridian's direct contracts with Green executed at a scale NationalCo's actuaries must now price, and answered — so far — with discounts, not structure.
env: MANDATORY W3 TRUST SHOCK (landed in-window): A venture-backed consumer appeals platform is exposed for mass-generating appeals with fabricated clinician attestations and unverifiable citations; days later a UM subcontractor breach exposes utilization-review records including algorithmic denial-score rationales. Congressional hearings target payer algorithms AND provider documentation AI; health-AI trust polling craters across the board. Patient-bot appeal volume drops roughly half from its high-single-digit peak and stays depressed for two turns, after which the W3 spec projects a litigation-oriented return (bots that auto-file AG complaints and demand provenance).

CMS POSTURE ROLL — STRICT (adverse to the currently leading side, per W3 requirement): With hearings making enforcement politically useful, CMS runs a 0057-F enforcement sweep — compliance notices and corrective-action exposure for plans that relied on good-faith attestation instead of live APIs. GovProgramCo's early build passes clean; several non-table payers and one table-adjacent regional book take notices; auto-pay appeal thresholds draw an audit-sampling advisory.

ANTITRUST ASYMMETRY: The FTC closes its civil investigative demand into the Blue coalition's denial-data utility with a no-action letter, expressly conditioned on the independent-manager restructuring; the same month, a payer's PBM acquisition clears with no conditions. The asymmetry is noted in a dissenting commissioner's statement and promptly ignored.

FEDERAL PREEMPTION WHIPSAW: The draft preemption executive order is signed — and enjoined within weeks by a district court in a coalition state. The previously stayed SB 1120-copy AI-UR statute resumes operationalization; other statehouses restart floor calendars cautiously. Compliance planners are now hedging both directions simultaneously.

COURTS (W3 venue-random): The magistrate in Meridian v. NationalCo orders production of ASO payment-integrity fee schedules and rotation-timing documents and grants NationalCo's counter-discovery into Meridian's documentation AI; an unpredicted partial unsealing puts a slice of the fee-structure material into trade press circulation, where Green's consultants and two state AGs read it.

MEDIA FLARE (1-turn, randomized target): A home-market story on an oncology patient's white-bagging denial-adjacent site-of-care redirection briefly singes RegionalMutual's transparency brand; the compact's documented good-faith record contains it within the cycle.

LABOR: Post-shock, payer SIU and clinical-reviewer hiring tightens as named-clinician review requirements spread (SB 1120-pattern statutes, GovProgramCo's protocol, Meridian's attestation workflow); reviewer compensation drifts up on both sides — a small, symmetric admin-cost tax the Vendor no longer fully captures.

turns.narrative: The final period ended not with a collision but with a convergence nobody wanted to name. NationalCo, reading two live flip conditions off its own ledger — unsealed fee schedules in AG hands and a direct-contracting bleed its actuaries could finally price — bought its way out of everything at once: the Meridian suit closed on process terms (reporting-and-trigger across COB, eligibility, and itemized-bill review, a narrowed eligibility-binding verification rider, mutual release, counter-discovery retired) days after a leaked expert-report excerpt alleging documentation-AI note inflation gave both parties a reason to sign quickly. Its Open-Book ASO chassis then executed Green's economics voluntarily — SaaS-default integrity fees, chosen auditors, full feeds — which is repricing, not surrender: the flat fee survives every state of the world, and the one rotation D3 still allowed went to specialty J-codes, OON repricing, and pharmacy-crossover COB, where roughly three quarters of yield banked before Green's 1/1/2030 taxonomy extension made the tail auditable on renewed accounts. Meridian's pharmacy alerts saw it land immediately; with no re-instrumentation point left, watching was all Blue could do — the doctrine's arithmetic, honestly applied. GovProgramCo quietly had the best turn at the table: Stars measure removals plus a lax CMS cycle let it re-intensify provider-facing MA integrity behind a pre-submission exchange now six categories wide, whose original two categories produced the game's first observed dispute-volume decline. RegionalMutual harvested its transparency franchise into mid-market account wins and signed both specialty-pharmacy disclosure instruments — cheap paper, since its residual trend moved into PBM and formulary economics no schedule reaches. Green's benchmark publication, cleared through the independent manager over a carrier complaint that drew a token FTC inquiry, supplied the second forcing event the consultant channel needed; Master Terms v3 landed into the last RFP season with NationalCo already conformed. The Vendor executed the only honest cure available: the appeals opco sale signed in 2029 and closed mid-2030, certification following at close — though Red's posted no-purchases wall stranded its technical engines off-table and the clearinghouse trust died unmourned when GovProgramCo declined to be the second depositor. The patient bots returned as predicted, angrier and provenance-hungry, auto-filing AG complaints that opened two inquiries into ASO payment-integrity practices — a bill that arrives after the game ends. Nothing at this table became industry infrastructure; several things became signed, operating, measurable machinery. That is what 2026–2030 could actually buy.
env: PATIENT-AI WEAPONIZED RETURN (W3 scripted; adverse to the currently leading side, Red): appeal bots return litigation-oriented in 2029 — auto-filing AG complaints with provenance attestations attached and demanding algorithm disclosure. Volume rebuilds toward the low-teens share of contested adverse determinations. Complaint streams plus the T2-unsealed fee schedules trigger two state AG inquiries into ASO payment-integrity fee practices at NationalCo; both are open, neither resolves in-game. Red's provenance fast-track riders channel certified appeals into clean SLAs, containing the operational hit but not the inquiry exposure.

CMS POSTURE ROLL — LAX: post-hearings budget exhaustion produces an understaffed CMS cycle — mass extensions on 0057-F corrective-action plans, slowed RADV pace, no new audit-sampling activity on auto-pay protocols. GovProgramCo's randomized fast-pay band never gets tested; laggard payers exhale; the enforcement whipsaw is now itself the pattern.

MEDIA HOSTILE STORY (randomized target: Blue): an expert-report excerpt from NationalCo's counter-discovery — alleging systematic 'note inflation' patterns in Meridian's documentation AI — leaks to trade press weeks before settlement. One-cycle flare per W3; Meridian's named-clinician attestation and provenance-audit architecture gives it a documented answer, and the story's chief effect is accelerating both parties to sign the release that retires the underlying record.

ANTITRUST ASYMMETRY (1-in-3 roll — HIT, buyer-side): a carrier trade association complaint frames Green's published PI-fee benchmark as coordinated price signaling; FTC opens a preliminary inquiry, finds the independent-manager form with White-imposed aggregation safeguards adequate at the preliminary stage, and leaves the file open. The same quarter, the Vendor's appeals-opco sale to a strategic buyer clears without a second request. The asymmetry is noted in a footnote nobody reads.

PREEMPTION WHIPSAW, CONTINUED: the appellate panel narrows the injunction against the federal preemption executive order on standing grounds but declines to stay the operational SB 1120-copy statute pending merits. Statehouses split into three camps — enact-and-wait, wait-and-see, and one repeal attempt. Compliance officers now budget for both regimes simultaneously as a permanent condition.

LABOR: named-clinician review mandates, provenance certification workflows, and both sides' attestation architectures keep clinical-reviewer compensation drifting upward; payer SIU talent begins migrating to provenance-verification and validation-infrastructure roles — the friction economy's workforce quietly reallocating from generating disputes to certifying their inputs.

Executed: reporting-and-trigger addendum on COB/eligibility/itemized-bill, eligibility-binding verification rider (COB carved out at the gate), scoped mutual release, counter-discovery retired. RegionalMutual signed the disclosure-and-protections form — cheap for a carrier whose commercial identity is transparency and whose own move already institutionalized continuity protections — but residual trend rotated into PBM/formulary economics the addendum cannot reach, and only 3-4 reporting quarters mature before scoring. Partial credit is the ceiling Lakeview itself predicted.

One bridge quarter of unworked Prairie denials occurred as priced. Summit's two-metro expansion was eased, ironically, by NationalCo's wrap product legitimizing carve-outs.

resolutions.move: NationalCo retention counterattack (Open-Book chassis, wrap product, litigation close-out)
resolutions.rationale: D3 §4(c) genuinely triggered — >5% of ASO book credibly exposed — so cooperation is ledger-gated, not goodwill. SaaS conversion locks fee revenue immune to reversal clawbacks by construction; wrap converts full-account losses into partial retentions that score better under the retention index; settlement on vacated-vector process terms costs little and retires ruling and AG-referral risk with two AGs reading unsealed schedules. Trade press read it as capitulation; the ledger reads it as repricing.

Approximately three quarters of fee yield banked clean on the ASO book (~20% take, no MLR drag per the payer economics brief); the tail became auditable only on accounts renewing to Green v3 taxonomy at 1/1/2030, a trim Red priced in advance. The exchange expansion to six categories is both admin-cost compression and the audit-defense exhibit; the original two categories showed the first measured dispute-volume decline per the 12-24 month IT clock — which also keeps flip condition (a) unsatisfied against Red permanently.

But the premise that no instrument reaches specialty pharmacy broke this turn: Lakeview's addendum and Green's rider now cover disclosure and site-of-care reporting, forcing the residual trend engine one ring further out into PBM/formulary economics. audit.worldModelFidelity: Strong. The record maps the W3 spec's 6-month turns onto three ~18-month macro turns and does so explicitly and consistently (e.g., 'T4-T6 sub-turn window = T2-T3 macro' for the shock). Every W3 obligation is discharged: (1) mandatory trust shock landed in-window at T2 (dual-sided — fabricated provider-bot attestations AND a payer UM breach), patient-bot volume halved for two turns, then returned weaponized/litigation-oriented at low-teens share, matching the spec's ~15% ceiling and rebound script; (2) CMS posture rolls produced all three states across the game (silent/contradictory T1, strict T2, lax T3) with the whipsaw itself becoming the pattern; (3) one hostile media story per turn with randomized/alternating targets cutting both ways (Vendor/Red deck leak T1, RegionalMutual white-bagging flare T2, Blue note-inflation leak T3); (4) antitrust asymmetry rigorously maintained — provider-side/buyer-side coordination drew a CID (T1) and an FTC benchmark inquiry (T3) while payer acquisitions cleared with light or no conditions all three turns, with the dissent/footnote color the spec implies; (5) federal preemption whipsaw ran the full arc (draft EO → stay of a state statute → EO signed and enjoined → appellate narrowing → permanent dual-regime budgeting) preserving the recurring 1-in-3 stay/chill risk; (6) courts behaved venue-randomly (partial screen trims, unpredicted partial unsealing, counter-discovery granted). The at-least-one-event-adverse-to-the-leader rule is clearly honored at T2 (strict CMS sweep) and T3 (weaponized bots + AG inquiries aimed at leading Red) but is ambiguous at T1. The W3 GREEN-passive language is superseded by Common Rules v2 making Green a first-class cell — a game-design override, not an adjudication infidelity.
downweightRecommendations: No material violations found; findings from this game do not require categorical down-weighting.

Down-weight the specific timing of the litigation-to-structural-settlement arc (Meridian v. NationalCo closing with process terms at ~3-3.5 years). Treat 'litigation produces process concessions inside a 4-5 year horizon' as a favorable-tail outcome dependent on W3 court randomness plus three simultaneous pressure sources, not a planning baseline; the base-rate band is settlement years 4-7 with only operational (not structural) effects reliably arriving at the discovery stage.

Down-weight the provenance-spec adoption speed (published to multi-payer riders and DOI reference in ~2 years). The scripted trust shock did the work; absent an equivalent exogenous scandal, voluntary-standard base rates (5-7 years to first production dyads) should govern any real-world inference about certification-layer plays.

Down-weight T1's negotiated-compact richness modestly when generalizing 'transparency compacts are attainable in year 1' — the record itself flags Blue got more than base rates predict, and the outcome depended on an idiosyncratic leak plus a visibly shopping jumbo account.

Retain at full weight the findings the record earned honestly against friction: rotation-outruns-instrumentation dynamics (Red's three-step vector rotation vs Blue's one-cycle re-instrumentation lag), the clawback-trigger arbitrage (fees rotated into never-reversing vectors), Green's procurement-as-enforcement channel binding only at renewal windows, the pre-submission exchange as the only dispute-shrinking instrument, and the clearinghouse trust dying exactly as voluntary-rail base rates predicted. These conclusions were repeatedly stress-tested against the base-rate table inside the record itself.

games.name: Regulatory Theater
games.seed: Both sides open with legal/regulatory strategy as their PRIMARY theater: Blue pursues state AI-UR legislation, litigation support, and evidence dossiers; Red pursues safe-harbor lobbying, preemption advocacy, and voluntary-standard preemption plays. Operational AI deployment continues on both sides but as the secondary front. What the regulatory environment actually delivers is governed strictly by the active world-model.

turns.narrative:
The opening eighteen months rewarded speed and punished exposure. Red's rotation was the cleanest play on the board: NationalCo swung its extraction engine from front-end clinical denials to post-pay itemized review and DRG downcoding on ASO books, and under asymmetric-friction physics nobody contested it — Meridian's rotation radar, declared in early 2026 and built on the fastest clock an AMC can roll, came online only in the closing months of 2027. Roughly four quarters of recoupment yield banked uncontested, booked as contingency fee revenue on employer money. Denial dashboards indexed on the vector Red abandoned showed flat-to-down front-end rates, which Red's lobbyists cited in every statehouse.

But the environment bit both directions, as this world does. An investigative series on legacy MA post-acute denials hit GovProgramCo despite its pre-emptive Stars firewall — the retreat shrank the surface, not the archive. The same season, DOJ opened a civil investigative demand into the Blue coalition's shared-services entity and benchmarking compact as buyer-side coordination, while RegionalMutual's license of NationalCo's PI toolset drew no letter. CMS, understaffed, opened an attestation pathway on 0057-F enforcement, devaluing Blue's compliance-watch file and NationalCo's early-shipper halo alike. Neither state bill cluster drew the feared preemption stay, so the statute clocks run — for now.

In the courts, Meridian's algorithmic-UM suit survived dismissal in narrowed form: contract and good-faith counts proceed, preemption trimmed the rest, discovery opens next turn. Green served CAA demand letters on all three carriers and filed against NationalCo when the ninety days ran.

Green was the quiet winner of the turn: the 25-account RFP wave launched with zero defections — Vendor sweeteners and Red's Fiduciary Partner Rider peeled off only non-coalition jumbos — the direct-contract pilot signed real paper with Meridian and Summit, and the conflict-disclosure standard forced the Vendor holdco to attest its both-sides ownership in writing, a document now sitting in two litigation files.

Blue's buy-side stumbled: Prairie's shared-service onboarding and Summit's AppealForge deployment each stalled a cycle despite engineered modifiers — pilot purgatory respects no term sheet. Meridian's own builds passed their milestones, but the appeals pilot arrives trained on edit-era denial data facing a post-pay world: effectiveness halved until re-instrumentation.

Vendor grew where Red spent and stalled where Blue stalled; its meters ran hardest on the very recoveries Green's clawback language will reach in 2028. Escalation is elevated, no D3 flip condition is live, and the scheduled trust shock has not yet arrived.
env: CMS posture roll (lax): facing the January 2027 CMS-0057-F deadline understaffed, CMS issues an attestation-based enforcement-discretion pathway for plans showing good-faith implementation — Blue's compliance-watch file yields little leverage this cycle, and NationalCo's early API shipment earns muted differentiation. Posture re-rolls next turn (1-in-3 strict sweep).

Hostile media event (target roll: GovProgramCo): a multi-part investigative series on MA post-acute AI denials runs against GovProgramCo, built from legacy case files predating its Stars firewall; congressional letters follow and CTM complaints spike in affected markets — mitigation shrank the surface, not the archive. Adverse-to-leader requirement satisfied against Red.

W3 antitrust asymmetry (roll hit, 1-in-3): DOJ opens a civil investigative demand into the Meridian-anchored shared-services entity and the Blue benchmarking compact as potential buyer-side coordination — the same season RegionalMutual's license of NationalCo's PI toolset closes without scrutiny. Compact diffusion freezes; Blue legal spend rises.

Labor-market event: a denial-economy talent war breaks open — Vendor poaches two senior SIU leaders, NationalCo files garden-leave litigation, and wages for experienced denial-management, coding, and SIU staff spike, nudging cost-per-touch upward (small, within bounds) for every cell.

Patient-AI trajectory (W3 volatile-growth phase, pre-shock): appeal-bot-assisted contests climb from the ~2% base toward high single digits of adverse determinations, concentrated in MA — marginal but compounding pressure on Red's cost per denial. The W3 mandatory trust-shock window has NOT yet opened; it looms in the next turn's range.

Binds only as executed ASO contract terms at 2028 renewals.

sign.detail: A unilateral purchasing condition: ownership disclosure, take-rate caps, fee-on-final-outcome, targeting-logic audit. Ordinary buyer power, no antitrust or UM-law defect. Adopted coalition-wide this turn.

sign.detail: As proposed — a certification body whose technical committee the interested vendor staffs and funds — it fails the legitimate-SDO test (Allied Tube, Hydrolevel). Converted to open-membership, published-procedure, appeal-rights SDO form with no vendor majority on the committee. Vendor's founding-funder position is recorded as a discoverable fact on the conflict ledger.

turns.narrative:
2028 was the turn the money moved and the ground shook. NationalCo executed the least intuitive play on the board: it signed Green's toughened Addendum v2 across the 25-account wave — retroactive fee audit and all — and in the same motion rebuilt its payment-integrity economics around fixed PEPM fees plus prevention-based shared savings on pre-pay avoided dollars, a fee base Green's clawback text cannot yet reach. Then it rotated a third time, out of post-pay review and upstream into pre-pay complex edits, eligibility validation, and documentation pends. Meridian's radar caught the shift within a quarter; its appeals engine, freshly re-tuned to post-pay, was mistargeted for the second consecutive cycle. The consolation was real: the legacy post-pay pipeline stayed contestable, and Meridian's clinical-validation unit banked strong overturns on top-decile downcodes — each reversal now a clawback exhibit under Green's new audit rights.

Then the mandatory shock arrived, and it wore the Vendor's logo. A breach in the holdco's legacy data lake — the enclave Bulkhead had not finished walling — spilled UR records with AI denial-score rationales alongside appeal drafts from the defense unit, proving the cross-flow both litigation files had circled. Health-AI trust cratered; patient-AI appeal volume halved; Congress convened hearings on payer denial algorithms and provider coding-intensity AI alike. CMS's posture roll came up strict: attestation audits swept 0057-F files and RegionalMutual drew a corrective action plan. In the statehouses, the preemption whipsaw chilled one bill cluster while the survivor enacted a hybrid statute — transparency, physician review, appeal SLAs — with Red's safe-harbor clause stripped on the hearing-room floor post-shock, leaving Red's own transparency architecture standing as the enforcement rail.

Blue's buy side finally cleared its rolls: Prairie and Summit both passed bought-down milestone checks, courtesy of vendor-at-risk paper that cost the Vendor money it suddenly needed elsewhere. GovProgramCo's dated gold-card announcement, launched before the shock, aged into the best-timed hedge of the game. Green ended the turn as architect: its addendum is live production paper, its CAA disgorgement theory survived dismissal in part, its clean-auditor standard is hiring, and its direct-contract channel now credibly exceeds five percent of NationalCo's book in one market. Entering 2029, flip conditions (b) and (c) are stacking against a payer that has already pre-paid for part of the peace; the open question is whether accommodation bought enough of it.
env: MANDATORY W3 TRUST SHOCK (window opened, shock fired): a breach in the Vendor holdco's legacy shared data lake — the enclave Project Bulkhead had not yet partitioned — exposes UR records including AI denial-score rationales from the PI unit alongside appeal drafts from the denial-defense unit, publicly proving the cross-unit data flow both litigation files had circled. Health-AI trust polling craters across payer, provider, and vendor AI alike; patient-AI appeal-tool usage drops roughly half for two turns, with a litigation-oriented, AG-complaint-filing rebound forecast for 2029.

Congressional hearings convene on the breach and run both ways per W3: payer denial algorithms and provider coding-intensity/documentation-AI practices are examined in the same sessions; GovProgramCo's dated pre-shock gold-card announcement and NationalCo's signed fiduciary addendum serve as defensive exhibits, while the Vendor holdco's lobbying record against dispute-shrinking reform surfaces in testimony.

CMS posture re-roll lands STRICT (1-in-3): an 0057-F attestation-file enforcement sweep, politically convenient post-shock. NationalCo's audit-ready files hold; RegionalMutual's slower stack draws a corrective action plan; GovProgramCo passes on APIs but collects continued post-acute audit attention. Posture re-rolls again T3.

Federal preemption whipsaw (1-in-3 per state regime): one of the two state AI-UR bill clusters is chilled by an appropriations-rider preemption threat and stalls; the surviving state enacts a hybrid statute — transparency, licensed-physician final review, appeal SLAs — stripping Red's safe-harbor clause on the floor post-shock and omitting corridor provisions as unenforceable.

W3 court randomness resolved: Meridian's discovery opens on schedule with preservation orders spanning the rotation window and a granted third-party compel of Vendor targeting logic (the breach mooted most objections); Green's CAA suit survives dismissal in part — disgorgement theory proceeds, prohibited-transaction count out — a Stern-pattern split rather than the J&J/Wells Fargo standing wall.

DOJ CID on the Blue benchmarking compact remains open despite the narrowed charter and cooperation; staff signals reduced scope but no closure — compact diffusion stays frozen while RegionalMutual's PI-toolset license again draws no scrutiny (W3 antitrust asymmetry).

Labor market: the garden-leave litigation over poached SIU leaders settles quietly on standard terms; denial-economy wages for coders, SIU, and appeals staff stay elevated, and the breach ignites a compliance-and-privacy talent scramble that nudges every cell's admin cost per touch upward (small, within bounds).

turns.narrative:
The final turn belonged to the ledgers, not the lawyers. NationalCo entered 2029 with both D3 flip conditions burning — litigation past discovery with an enacted statute behind it, and a direct-contract channel past five percent of book — and did what the doctrine predicts: it bought peace twice, scoped both purchases, and rotated the moment the ink dried. The Meridian settlement executed the Pre-Adjudication All-Vector Process Compact: machine-readable edit logic, same-specialty clinical validation, interest-bearing unwind of reversed recoupments, and the 60-day change-notice clause Blue spent two turns learning to write. The Green settlement traded audited fee refunds and Addendum v3 execution for three-year ASO extensions — after White severed the direct-contract standstill as foreclosure no employer counsel signs. The prevention-fee shelter died at one year old; the negotiated seam was PEPM base pricing, disclosed but uncapped, exactly the visible-price trade Green had said it would accept. Then came the fourth rotation: out of clinical adjudication altogether, into COB, subrogation, and contract-compliance pricing edits. The change-notice clause did its single job — the new vector deployed warned rather than shadowed — but Meridian's twice-retuned clinical appeals machinery has no grip on pricing-edit disputes, and Red banked a lower-cents, quieter yield stream that Blue could see and not yet fight.

Lakeview finally spent its leverage: hedge executed first, then Rider v1.1 signed all-lines inside a three-year renewal a CAP-chastened RegionalMutual could show CMS as remediation. The Green cell executed anyway; the strand failed. Prairie's complaint mill and Summit's gold-card qualification harvested real but bounded gains — year-one statute enforcement ran symbolic, per the base rate, and single digits of Summit's groups cleared the look-back thresholds. GovProgramCo quietly enjoyed the game's largest exogenous gift as the Stars overhaul deleted the complaints and appeals measures from its risk ledger.

The environment stayed W3 to the end. CMS rolled contradictory guidance that briefly tangled the CAP closure. Patient-AI returned weaponized, auto-filing AG complaints against statute SLAs. The DOJ CID closed with a warning — two years too late for the benchmarking compact. And the turn's mandatory adverse event found the leader: a national story on employer steerage put Green's fast-lane benefit design on the front page, and its first measured direct-contract readout came in small and mixed, right on the underdelivery base rate. The Vendor cut itself in half to sell the pieces, converted its book to compliance SaaS, and left the conflict that built it capitalized in a litigation box. Peace, where it arrived, was priced — never given.
env: CMS posture re-roll lands SILENT/CONTRADICTORY (1-in-3): overlapping subregulatory guidance on 0057-F API audit scope and MA post-pay clinical-validation review points in opposite directions within one quarter; RegionalMutual's CAP closure is delayed a quarter by the ambiguity before acceptance; no enforcement sweep occurs and no one can plan against the file.

Patient-AI rebound arrives WEAPONIZED per the post-shock W3 trajectory: appeal-bot volume recovers to pre-breach levels and beyond in litigation-oriented form — tools now auto-file statute-SLA grievances and AG complaints alongside appeals; three state AGs open inquiries seeded by bot-generated complaint dockets; Red's cost per adverse determination rises and the enacted statute becomes the bots' citation engine.

Mandatory adverse-to-leader event targets GREEN: a national investigative feature on employer benefit-design steerage ('your employer's plan chose your hospital') runs multi-outlet, built on member-abrasion anecdotes from the fast-lane cost-share design; a congressional letter goes to coalition anchor employers; Green's member-friction metric takes the hit its move sheet pre-accepted, at higher public volume than budgeted.

W3 antitrust asymmetry, final installment: DOJ closes the Blue benchmarking-compact CID with a warning letter and no action — two turns of frozen diffusion never to be recovered — while in the same season a non-table carrier's acquisition of a mid-market PI vendor clears review without a second request.

Court randomness: the Meridian and Green settlements are approved without incident, but a copycat CAA fiduciary suit is filed against GovProgramCo by a non-coalition employer using Green's open-licensed document stack — the template's litigation-exhibit diffusion vector firing outside its authors' control.

Labor market: Vendor separation releases SIU, appeals, and compliance staff into the market, easing denial-economy wage pressure slightly for the first time in the game; demand rotates toward statute-compliance and audit talent, where wages stay hot.
