signposts: Whether the two external purchaser coalitions' Addendum v3 executions convert to signed carrier paper at 1/1/2031 renewals — the test of whether Green built market infrastructure or a coalition artifact.
The state implementing rulemaking's final text (2030-31): if the clinical-validation and machine-readable denial-code modules survive, Rider v1.1's diffusion clock compresses from 10-15 years to 5-7.
NationalCo's fifth fee architecture: watch ASO base-administration price loading and carrier-owned 'clinical value' service lines for the shelter v3's disposition-linked definition cannot reach.

Whether pricing-edit and COB disputes grow their own contest infrastructure — the non-clinical vector is uncontested today because nobody has built appeals tooling for it, not because the recoveries are all clean.
PI-unit sale closing versus collapse on litigation-liability allocation — the difference between a remediated exit and a stranded asset wearing a litigation box.
AG inquiries seeded by bot complaint dockets converting to enforcement actions in 2031 — the weaponized patient-AI channel is now the fastest-moving regulatory input in the system.
Lakeview's leakage and margin trend through 2030-31 as the cleanest natural experiment on whether executed process terms actually move provider economics or merely document them.
Second direct-contract cohort readout: a repeat of the small-mixed result validates the underdelivery base rate and lets carriers reprice the defection threat down accordingly.

resolutions.move: Meridian re-instrumentation to pre-pay vector plus first-pass clean-claim integrity layer
resolutions.rationale: D3 1.3: Red's fourth rotation (declared same turn, immediate effect) beat a same-turn re-instrumentation; the pre-built rotation radar cut the shadow to ~1 quarter but Meridian's clinical appeals stack has no competency on COB/subrogation/pricing-edit disputes, so detection did not equal contestation. First-pass integrity still bites: evidence brief supports ~$57/claim rework avoided and 69% of claims-AI adopters reporting reduced denials; pend/eligibility leakage improvement held inside the ±2pt bound (3.3).

resolutions.move: Meridian settle-for-structure: All-Vector Process Compact as settlement consideration
resolutions.rationale: D3 §4 flip conditions (b) and (c) both satisfied on NationalCo's own ledger — the only condition under which Red signs. Settlement landed inside the litigation clock (filed T1, ruling/settlement window T+5-6). Every compact term sits on the checklist safe list (items 6-10). Blue traded the low-probability bad-faith jackpot for signed structure; the change-notice clause converted the next rotation from a 2-turn shadow into a 60-day warned contest — notice, not prohibition, which is why Red could sign it.

resolutions.move: Lakeview renewal strike: Rider v1.1 execution with Green direct-contract hedge
resolutions.rationale: Common Rules 3.2: renewal is the binding window and this was it. The CAP, the NationalCo compact precedent set weeks earlier, and an executed walk-away hedge supplied §4(b)-scale pressure at regional scale. Ruled outcome merges the packages: Rider v1.1 all-lines including the clinical-validation module, rate floor honored, RegionalMutual takes a 3-year term as its retention consideration — face-saving frame accepted by both sides.

resolutions.move: Prairie/Summit enforcement-rail harvest: statute complaints, gold-card qualification, rulemaking dossier
resolutions.rationale: Base-rate table: statute effective-date to measurable behavior change is 2-5 years and symbolic compliance is the modal year-one outcome — Prairie's complaint log prices exposure into Red's ledger but produces no fines of consequence in-window. Gold-card rule enforced: single-digit share of Summit's groups qualify year one; recaptured PA hours are real but bounded. Rulemaking dossier scores as milestone progress only per 4(C); regulation text cannot bind before 2030-31.

resolutions.move: NationalCo Settle-and-Retain: Green settlement as retention transaction
resolutions.rationale: Retention — a scored Red metric — locked via 3-year extensions across the coalition wave, and the disgorgement tail extinguished pre-ruling per D3 litigation physics. But the standstill clause was struck as severable foreclosure, Addendum v3 execution was extracted as consideration (killing the prevention-fee shelter after one year), and the refund precedent is now quoted in every purchaser negotiation. Red bought what it needed at a price that compresses PI yield.

resolutions.move: NationalCo fourth rotation into non-clinical PI plus Avoided-Savings Verification Protocol
resolutions.rationale: D3 1.2: rotation immediate, and the choice of vector was doctrinally clean — COB/subrogation/pricing edits sit outside the AI-UM statute, outside the settled clinical theories, and outside Blue's appeals competency; ~2 quarters of effectively uncontested yield banked despite radar detection. But cents-per-dollar is structurally lower, the compact's change-notice clause forced disclosed deployment, and the verification protocol was superseded by v3's stronger sponsor-auditor regime — the preemption gambit failed even as the rotation worked.

resolutions.move: GovProgramCo Stars-overhaul arbitrage with statute worn as compliance moat
resolutions.rationale: The economics brief is explicit that removal of CTM/appeals/disenrollment measures (2027 measurement year, 2029 Stars) materially lowers the Stars price of MA friction — an exogenous tailwind landing exactly this turn. Electronic PA at ~$0.05 vs ~$3.50 manual makes statute-compliant automation nearly free at the margin. The NAIC model-rule petition is routed to the milestone ledger and cannot mature by 2030 (3-7 yr lag); the weaponized patient-AI rebound and continued post-acute audits keep residual exposure but not Stars-linked.

resolutions.move: RegionalMutual regional lockdown: CAP cure, Lakeview renewal, Vendor MSA renegotiation, strand the Green cell
resolutions.rationale: Three of four legs landed: CAP cured (one quarter late, tangled by CMS's contradictory guidance), Lakeview locked for 3 years, and the Vendor take-rate cut hard at its post-breach nadir with first-look rights on the PI-unit sale. The strand failed — the Green-Lakeview bilateral executed anyway because the hedge preceded the renewal, and the process price of the renewal was full Rider v1.1, well beyond the statute-mirror terms RegionalMutual planned to concede.

resolutions.move: Addendum v3 at the 2029 RFP cycle: close the avoided-dollar loophole
resolutions.rationale: Purchaser money-attached diffusion is the only fast lane the base-rate table recognizes (CAQH-analog), and flip-condition leverage made declining the 25-account book irrational for NationalCo. Executed with one negotiated seam White records as commercial, not signability: disposition-linked fees (contingency plus prevention/shared-savings) fall under the 15% aggregate cap with counterfactual validation and avoided-then-paid fee reversal; PEPM base allocable to PI is disclosed and auditable but uncapped — the visible-price trade Green's own move sheet accepted.

resolutions.move: Retroactive fee audit executed and converted into the NationalCo settlement
resolutions.rationale: The audit-to-refund pipeline delivered hard dollars — the only kind 3.6 credits — targeted by Meridian's overturn exhibits; the surviving disgorgement count plus a quantified audit matured inside the game clock where a verdict could not. Open demand letters against RegionalMutual and GovProgramCo retained as pricing comparators; a copycat external suit filed on Green's own open-licensed template is the diffusion vector working, at the cost of losing control of it.

resolutions.move: Direct-contract tranche 3, benefit-design steerage, Lakeview cell execution, measured cohort readout
resolutions.rationale: The chronic-underdelivery base rate held: the first clean-auditor cohort readout came in small and mixed — enough to earn the game's first (small) measured-savings credit, not enough to validate the channel. Steerage made the volume threat real in two markets above 5% but triggered the W3 adverse-to-leader media event and a measurable member-friction hit Green accepted in advance. Lakeview bilateral executed over RegionalMutual's counter-offer.

resolutions.move: Vendor re-entry conditions and open-licensing of the Green standards stack
resolutions.rationale: PE exit pressure made audited-wall terms extractable now and worthless later, exactly as Green's move sheet priced it — the separated AppealForge qualified, the PI unit remains conditional. Two external purchaser coalitions executed derivative Addendum/disclosure language from the model library, clearing the early-external-adopter test White set at T2. Fiduciary defensibility now rests on market-standard status, the strongest CAA posture available.

resolutions.move: Bulkhead II: full legal separation and dual-track exit launch
resolutions.rationale: Corporate separation completed inside the 18-month clock with the litigation-liability box capitalized at the legacy holdco — the remediated fact pattern buyers require. But neither exit consummated by end-2030: AppealForge's process is open on locked renewals, the PI-unit LOI pends the liability-allocation fight. Per 4(C), partial credit for milestones reached; no credit for the projected multiple.

resolutions.move: Compliance Rail: statute-conformance suite and prevention-fee audit schema
resolutions.rationale: The conformance suite anchored real flat-fee ARR — RegionalMutual under its CAP and GovProgramCo buying audit armor — because the statute converted process obligations into mandatory spend with no immunity attached. The schema land-grab was not captured: Green folded the published methodology into v3 royalty-free and kept its clean flat-fee auditor on the engagement; Vendor supplied the ruler and someone else holds it.

resolutions.move: AppealForge pre-pay pivot and multi-year renewal lock-in
resolutions.rationale: D3 1.3 rotation-beats-deployment struck a third time: the Pre-Pay Defense Module shipped into a vector NationalCo was vacating; the eligibility-validation component retains value against the COB/eligibility overlap but the pend-clearing core is half-mistargeted, and Vendor owns the miss under at-risk terms. The renewals — the actual exit asset — locked: 3-year terms with Prairie shared services, Summit, and the Lakeview land.

resolutions.move: Lobbying reversal: compliance-rail advocacy, CIPAS sunset
resolutions.rationale: The posture flip is economically coherent post-separation — statute diffusion now grows TAM instead of shrinking it — and closing the CIPAS founding-funder entry removed the last live Allied Tube-pattern exhibit before diligence. Called opportunistic in hearings and plaintiff briefs, as Vendor priced; survivable, and worth more in the sale deck than it costs on the stand.

turns.bluePosture: CONVERT AND CONSOLIDATE. Blue enters the final turn holding leverage it has never held before: Meridian's litigation is past discovery with preservation orders spanning the rotation window and compelled Vendor targeting logic; the surviving state statute's enforcement window opens this turn with Red's own transparency architecture as the rail; RegionalMutual sits under a CMS corrective action plan; Green's direct-contract channel has crossed the 5% flip threshold in one NationalCo market; and — for the first time — all four archetypes have live, stall-cleared operational capability. D3 flip conditions (b) and (c) are stacked. Blue's posture is therefore not escalation (symmetric escalation only inflates our own admin cost per 3.5) but conversion: trade litigation and regulatory exposure for signed, ROTATION-COVERED process instruments while attacking leakage at its new source. Red has rotated to pre-pay pends and eligibility friction — which is the one vector Blue can defeat upstream, by perfecting claims before submission rather than fighting denials after. Operationally we re-instrument once, correctly, to the pre-pay vector and stop chasing; legally we settle for structure, not damages; and every cooperative instrument we table covers ALL denial vectors with prospective change-notice, because D3 scoped-cooperation doctrine has taught us twice that a compact covering one vector is an invitation to rotate to the next.

turns.redPosture: CONSOLIDATE THE ARCHITECTURE, PRICE THE PEACE, KEEP THE YIELD MOVING. Turn 3 is scoring season: Red's job is not to win new fights but to lock in what it already built before the clocks stop. Two D3 flip conditions are genuinely live against NationalCo — Meridian's litigation is past discovery with an enacted statute behind it (condition b), and Green's direct-contract channel credibly exceeds 5% of book in one market (condition c). Doctrine says a rational payer now signs scoped instruments on the contested vectors and rotates yield to what the instruments do not cover. So Red settles narrowly and expensively-looking-but-cheap: it converts litigation and defection risk into multi-year ASO retention paper (retention is a scored metric; a lost jumbo dwarfs the PI fees on it), pre-emptively hands Green auditability of the prevention-fee base before Green's 2029 RFP cycle drafts something worse, and executes a fourth rotation — out of clinical UM entirely, into non-clinical eligibility/COB/subrogation/contract-compliance vectors that sit outside the AI-UM statute's scope, outside Meridian's clinical-validation strength, and outside Green's clawback text, which is keyed to appeal-reversed clinical recoveries. Meanwhile GovProgramCo arbitrages the CMS Stars overhaul (complaints/appeals/disenrollment measures exit with the 2027 measurement year, cutting the Stars price of MA friction exactly as this turn's measurement window opens) while wearing the enacted statute — Red's own stripped template — as a compliance moat. RegionalMutual plays pure defense: cure the CAP, lock the regional book at the Lakeview renewal, and kill Green's Lakeview direct-contract cell in diligence. No cartoon aggression: every dollar of new friction this turn must be non-clinical, statute-compliant, and fee-based on ASO.
